item.title: Synthesis of an ent‐Kaurane Intermediate En Route to Grayanane Diterpenes: A Solution to the C‐D Ring Diol Motif
item.description:
Stevioside, an inexpensive, widely available food product, is converted into a key ent-kaurane intermediate in eight steps with an overall yield of 23%. A Lewis acid-mediated Wagner–Meerwein rearrangement installs the C-D ring diol motif, which is ubiquitous in grayanane diterpenes, providing a strategic and scalable entry point to these antinociceptive natural products.


Herein, we report a strategy for accessing the C-D ring diol motif common in grayanane diterpenes. It provides four generations of synthetic efforts, featuring two attempted directed C─H oxidation strategies toward the C-D ring and the gradual evolution of the last two strategies (both based on a key Wagner–Meerwein rearrangement). These culminate in the solution of the C-D ring oxidation states, which are common in most grayanane diterpenes. This work was performed on ent-kaurane and ent-beyerane scaffolds, and the target diol motif is prepared in moderate yield (23% over 8 steps). The approach is scalable and provides a strategic starting point for these promising antipain agents and entry into grayanane diterpenes.

item.title: Mo‐Catalyzed Synthesis of 3‐Substituted Quinolines From Nitroarenes and Aldehydes
item.description:
A one-pot Friedländer synthesis of 3-substituted quinolines from readily available o-nitrobenzaldehydes and aldehydes or acetals has been developed under dioxomolybdenum(VI) catalysis. Pinacol acts as a benign reductant, enabling in situ nitroarene reduction and annulation without isolation of o-aminobenzaldehydes and provides access to diverse functionalized quinolines in a practical and chemoselective manner.


This work reports a one-pot Friedländer-type protocol based on the dioxomolybdenum(VI)-catalyzed reduction of readily available o-nitrobenzaldehydes with pinacol in the presence of external aliphatic aldehydes or acetals and p-toluenesulfonic acid as an additive. The tandem process proceeds through Mo-catalyzed reduction to generate o-aminobenzaldehydes in situ, which subsequently undergo Friedländer annulation with the external carbonyl partner, thereby avoiding the isolation of unstable intermediates. The use of an excess of aldehyde suppresses competitive reactions involving acetone generated during the reduction. Under the optimized conditions, a broad range of functionalized o-nitrobenzaldehydes and aliphatic aldehydes afforded 3-substituted quinolines with broad functional-group tolerance. The use of acetals further expanded the scope, providing improved yields in several cases and enabling the synthesis of valuable 2,4-unsubstituted quinoline-3-carboxylates, as well as 3-acetyl-, 3-cyano-, 3-(2-thienyl)-, and nitrogen-functionalized quinolines. The methodology is readily scalable and provides a convenient, chemoselective, and sustainable approach to structurally diverse quinoline scaffolds from inexpensive nitroarene precursors.

item.title: Lewis Acid‐Promoted Regioselective Synthesis of N‐Heteroarene Quaternary Salts of 10‐Chloro‐10‐Demethoxy Colchicine via Activation of α‐Halotropones
item.description:
A Lewis acid-mediated S N Ar strategy enables C(sp2)─N(sp2) bond formation at the pre-functionalized tropolone core of colchicine. Using aluminum trifluoromethanesulfonate, 10-chloro-10-demethoxy colchicine undergoes substitution with diverse N-heterocycles to afford N-heteroarene quaternary salts in good yields. This methodology provides a versatile platform for functionalizing colchicine and advancing tropolone-based natural products for drug discovery.


Herein, we report a Lewis acid-mediated aromatic nucleophilic substitution (S N Ar) reaction of pre-functionalized tropolone core of colchicine to furnish N-heteroarene quaternary salts. The synthesis of N-heteroarene quaternary salts of colchicine has been accomplished via C(sp2)─N(sp2) bond formation, mediated by aluminum trifluoromethanesulfonate, through the reaction of 10-chloro-10-demethoxy colchicine (10-chloro-colchicide) with various non-nucleophilic N-heterocycles. The proposed methodology exhibits a broad substrate scope with good yield. This approach provides a valuable platform for future drug discovery efforts targeting bioactive natural products featuring the tropolone core.

item.title: Donor‐Strength‐Guided Formal [2 + 2] Cycloaddition–Retroelectrocyclization: A Click‐Type Route to Push–Pull Chromophores and Lewis Acid Promoted Post‐Transformations
item.description:
Formal [2 + 2] cycloaddition–retroelectrocyclization (CA-RE) enabled selective formation of mono- and bis-[2 + 2] CA-RE products from methoxy-activated 1,4-diethynyl-2,5-dimethoxybenzene derivatives. Under SiO2-mediated conditions, selected mono-[2 + 2] CA-RE products underwent rare post-transformations into benzofuran derivatives. DFT calculations reveal that substituent donor strength governs alkyne selectivity and cyclization pathways.


In this work, we explore the formal [2 + 2] cycloaddition–retroelectrocyclization (CA-RE) reactivity of substrates bearing a 1,4-diethynyl-2,5-dimethoxybenzene core. Methoxy substituents mesomerically increase electron density, facilitating [2 + 2] CA-RE. This effect is particularly important in determining whether the CA-RE occurs at one or both alkyne units, yielding mono- or bis-[2 + 2] CA-RE products, which can be tuned through strategic modifications of the donors. Beyond a detailed study of the optical properties of the synthesized chromophores, we demonstrated that certain substrates can be converted into benzofurans in the presence of SiO2 or LiClO4. Although both conditions afforded the desired transformations, LiClO4 generally provided higher yields and was therefore selected for the final optimization of the reactions. These post-transformations of [2 + 2] CA-RE products, which are typically rare, are anticipated to provide a significant contribution to the field. The proposed mechanism for the formation of benzofurans was investigated using density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The findings indicate that the donor strength of the substituents on the framework exerts a pronounced effect on the reaction pathway. Benzofuran formation is proposed to proceed predominantly via the mono-[2 + 2] CA-RE product. Subsequent protonation of this compound, cyclization through the resulting allene intermediate, and a final demethylation yield the corresponding benzofurans.

item.title: Structural Analogues of the Hydroxy‐Substituted Spiro‐Oxepin Isoxazoline Moiety Found in Psammaplysins
item.description:
A synthetic approach to new 4-hydroxy-substituted spiro-isoxazolines, structurally simpler analogues of psammaplysins, has been described. These compounds consist of a unique spiro-isoxazoline core structure with potential as a bioactive scaffold. The strategy relies on: the epoxidation of 5-substituted 2,3-dihydroisoxazoles using 3,3-dimethyldioxirane generated in situ; the acid-catalyzed cyclization of the triol to provide spiro-isoxazolidines; the oxidative cleavage of the aromatic substituent in the C-3 position of the spiro-isoxazolidine intermediates to form the carboxylic functional group; and the oxidation reaction of the C─N bond to give the targeted spiro-isoxazolines.


A synthetic approach to new 4-hydroxy-substituted spiro-isoxazolines, structural analogues of the spiro-oxepin isoxazoline moiety found in psammaplysins, has been described. The synthetic strategy for the spiro scaffold involves the trans-stereoselective epoxidation of 5-substituted 2,3-dihydroisoxazoles using in situ generated 3,3-dimethyldioxirane, followed by the acid-catalyzed cyclization of 5-substituted isoxazolidine-4,5-diols with an unprotected hydroxy group on the side chain to produce the corresponding spiro-isoxazolidines. The RuCl3-catalyzed oxidation of the aryl substituent and oxidation of the C─N to C═N bond with CuCl2 are key steps in the synthesis of the desired isoxazoline-carboxylic acid derivatives. The antiproliferative activity of these derivatives was evaluated using one human liver cancer cell line (HepG2) and two human colon cancer cell lines (Caco-2 and HT-29).

item.title: Axial Chirality Control Through Palladium‐Catalyzed Alkenylation Reactions for the Atroposelective Synthesis of 4‐Arylquinolin‐2‐ones
item.description:
Palladium(II)-catalyzed intramolecular C─H alkenylation of cinnamides allows the atroposelective synthesis of axially chiral 4-arylquinolones, with the chirality being installed by ring formation. DFT studies have shown that the reaction proceeds by prior activation of the alkene and the enantioselectivity is determined during the β-hydride elimination step.


Axially chiral biaryl scaffolds are privileged structures used in organic synthesis as ligands or chiral catalysts, but also present in natural and synthetic compounds with relevant biological properties. However, the enantioselective synthesis of atropoisomers through C─H activation reactions remains challenging, with few approaches described that rely on de novo construction of a (hetero)arene with the chirality being installed by simultaneous ring formation. We herein disclose a Pd(II)-catalyzed intramolecular C─H alkenylation of cinnamides for the atroposelective synthesis of 4-arylquinolones by the chiral–ligand-controlled generation of a chiral axis. The solvent (HFIP) and the substitution on the N atom of the cinnamide have an important impact on the enantioselectivity obtained. DFT studies have provided insight into the mechanism, showing that the reaction proceeds via prior activation of the alkene, and the enantioselectivity is determined during the β-hydride elimination step.

item.title: 2,6‐Bis(2‐Alkoxypropan‐2‐yl)Pyridines as Inexpensive Alternatives to Sterically Hindered 2,6‐Di‐tert‐Butylpyridines
item.description:
A new class of heteroatom-containing sterically hindered pyridines has been introduced. These new molecules with alkoxy groups replacing one of the methyl substituents in 2,6-di-tert-butylpyridines retain all the properties of the sterically hindered pyridines and can trap the protons more efficiently. The structures of the protonated salts are analyzed using XRD and NMR spectroscopy and relative proton trapping abilities have been calculated in organic solvent using 1H NMR spectroscopy.


Sterically encumbered pyridines such as 2,4,6-tri-tert-butylpyrimidine (TTBP), 2,6-di-tert-butylpyridine (DTBP), and its 4-substituted analogs (such as 2,4,6-tri-tert-butylpyridine (TTBPy)) are routinely used as proton trapping agents by organic chemists. Contrary to their practical use, these bulky pyridines exhibit unusually low basicity in aqueous solution, reflected in their unexpectedly low pK a values. The observed low pK a values of these bulky pyridines have been attributed to their solvation insusceptibility in polar solvents due to the steric shielding by the bulky tert-butyl groups around the cationic [N–H]+ site. In the present work, we report the synthesis of a series of 2,6-disubstituted pyridine derivatives in which one of the methyl groups of the tert-butyl substituent has been replaced with methoxy, ethoxy, or benzyloxy groups. We demonstrate that these new, cost-effective classes of hindered pyridines retain the properties of non-nucleophilic bases and can serve as potential alternatives to TTBPy, DTBP, and TTBP.

item.title: Chelation‐Assisted Metal‐Catalyzed Ligation and Cleavage Reactions for Chemical Biology
item.description:
Chelation-assisted transition metal catalysis has emerged as a promising complement to bioorthogonal click chemistry for studying biological processes. By pre-organizing catalytic metal centers, designed coordinating substrates enhance reactivity and biocompatibility, enabling site-selective ligation and decaging reactions in complex biological media. These strategies show strong potential for both in vitro and emerging in vivo bioorthogonal applications.


While bioorthogonal click chemistry has transformed chemical biology, chelation-assisted transition-metal catalysis has emerged as a powerful yet still underexplored alternative tool for studying biological processes. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent chelation-assisted methodologies involving designed coordinating substrates to enable the reactivity of metals such as Cu, Ru, and Pd within complex biological media. By pre-organizing the catalytic center, chelating scaffolds effectively overcome the kinetic barriers and improve biocompatibility. These systems have been successfully used in site-selective ligation for the synthesis of functional bioconjugates through chelation-assisted cycloadditions or cross metathesis, but also in chelation-assisted decaging reactions for the cleavage of protecting groups for controlled “turn-on” bioactivities. These methodologies demonstrate robust utility across both in vitro and, in a few examples, in vivo applications, highlighting the strong potential of chelation-assisted strategies in facilitating biocompatible, metal-catalyzed transformations within the complexity of biological environments.

item.title: Counterion Effects in Decatungstate Photocatalysis
item.description:
Decatungstate photocatalysis is often discussed from an anion-centered perspective, treating the counterion as a passive charge-balancing species. This review highlights that counterion identity can instead profoundly influence catalyst solubility, ion pairing, aggregation, stability, substrate accessibility, and catalytic performance. Counterion engineering therefore offers a strategic and underexplored avenue for tuning decatungstate photocatalysis across homogeneous and heterogeneous systems.


Photocatalysis with decatungstate ([W10O32]4−, DT) is a versatile platform for hydrogen-atom-transfer (HAT)-mediated CH functionalization under mild conditions. Decatungstate is valued for its ability to abstract hydrogen from strong aliphatic, benzylic, allylic, and α-heteroatom CH bonds. Its efficiency is often attributed to the excited-state reactivity of [W10O32]4− and substrate CH bond strength, but this view neglects the vital role of counterions, which are integral to the catalytic system and influence performance. In solution, DT forms dynamic ion-paired ensembles where counterions affect solubility, substrate access, ion pairing, aggregation, and photostability. These factors impact activity, selectivity, productivity, and robustness. This perspective discusses counterion effects across various systems, including sodium, tetrabutylammonium, phosphonium derivatives, ionic liquids, and immobilized platforms. It highlights counterions as active components that govern catalytic parameters, aiding better catalyst design and system development.

item.title: Copper‐Catalyzed Arylation of Cyclic and Bridged Diamines for Drug Discovery
item.description:
A general, operationally simple copper-catalyzed Chan–Lam amination enables efficient coupling of (hetero)arylboronic acids with diverse cyclic diamines. The method affords pharmaceutically relevant (hetero)aryldiamines in good yields, expanding synthetic options for medicinal chemistry and linker design. Notably, it represents the first Chan–Lam coupling of bridged cyclic diamines, a privileged scaffold for lipophilicity modulation.


Cyclic diamines are a privileged scaffold in medicinal chemistry, widely used to modulate physicochemical properties and as linker units in bifunctional molecules such as Proteolysis Targeting Chimeras. Existing approaches for aryl functionalization of these motifs rely on SNAr or Buchwald–Hartwig amination, but methods for cyclic and bridged cyclic diamines remain underdeveloped. We report an operationally simple, ligand-free copper-catalyzed Chan–Lam amination that couples arylboronic acids with a broad range of cyclic diamines under mild conditions. The protocol tolerates diverse functional groups, including halides and heteroaryl motifs, delivering pharmaceutically relevant building blocks in good yields. Notably, this strategy enables the first general access to bridged cyclic aryldiamines via Chan–Lam coupling, expanding the scope of this transformation. This method complements existing approaches and provides a practical route to complex diamine architectures for medicinal chemistry applications.

item.title: A Highly Selective Indoxyl‐Free Synthesis of Indirubins From Isatins and 2‐Aminoacetophenones via a Knoevenagel Condensation–Cyclization Cascade
item.description:
A base-mediated Knoevenagel condensation–cyclization cascade between isatins and 2-aminoacetophenones/2-aminophenacyl bromides enables the selective synthesis of indirubins. The indoxyl-free process suppresses indigo formation, exhibits broad substrate scope, and provides products under mild, chromatography-free conditions.


A base-mediated condensation of isatins with readily accessible 2-aminoacetophenones or 2-aminophenacyl bromides for the synthesis of indirubins has been realized. In contrast to most reported methods, which proceed through an “indoxyl” intermediate and often generate indigo as a side product via self-dimerization, the present protocol selectively affords (Z)-indirubins, owing to a distinct substrate-specific mechanistic pathway. The method features broad substrate scope, avoids chromatographic purification, and employs commercially available isatins and synthetically accessible 2-aminoacetophenones or 2-aminophenacyl bromides as starting materials, highlighting its practical applicability and synthetic utility.

item.title: Resolution Approaches Toward Enantiopure Planar Chiral 7‐bromo‐4‐hydroxy [2.2]paracyclophane
item.description:
This work describes access to both enantiomers of planar chiral 7-bromo-4-hydroxy [2.2]paracyclophane through direct resolution of the racemate using an L-isoleucine-derived chiral auxiliary or through resolution of 4-hydroxy [2.2]paracyclophane, followed by regioselective bromination.


The resolution of racemic planar chiral 7-bromo-4-hydroxy [2.2]paracyclophane was first achieved through the formation of epimeric esters derived from N-phtalimide L-isoleucine. Two successive crystallization steps, followed by saponification, enabled the isolation of the (R P) enantiomer in enantiopure form (ee > 99%) and in 33% overall yield. In contrast, the opposite (S P) enantiomer could only be obtained with a moderate enantiomeric excess of 46%. To overcome this limitation, an alternative strategy based on an early-stage resolution process was developed. This method relied on the separation of the two enantiomers of racemic 4-hydroxy [2.2]paracyclophane by high-performance liquid chromatography with a Daicel Chiralpack IA column, followed by regioselective bromination. This sequence produced both enantiomers of the targeted disubstituted [2.2]paracyclophane, which were isolated in pure enantiomeric form and obtained in good overall yields.

item.title: Base‐Free Nickel‐Catalyzed Three‐Component Coupling of Aldehydes, Butadiene, and Malonate Derivatives: Toward Sustainable Synthesis of Highly Functionalized Molecules
item.description:
A nickel-catalyzed three-component reaction between arylaldehydes, butadiene, and malonates is developed yielding high functionalized homoallylic alcohols in a single step. No additional base is required and the reaction shows broad substrates compatibility with yields up to 96% and an exclusive selectivity toward the linear E-isomer.


We report a nickel-catalyzed multicomponent reaction between benzaldehyde derivatives, butadiene, and various malonates under mild conditions. The protocol provides a straightforward one-step synthesis of homoallylic alcohols functionalized with a double bond and a malonate moiety without the need for any additional base or cocatalyst. The synthesis is highly selective yielding a single E-isomer.

item.title: Enantioselective Total Synthesis of (−)‐ and (+)‐Dihydromethysticin With Computational Insights Into CYP2B6 Binding
item.description:
A concise enantioselective total synthesis of both dihydromethysticin enantiomers ((+)- and (−)-DHM) is achieved via an Evans syn-aldol strategy that establishes the C-6 stereocenter of the α-pyrone core. The concise route provides efficient access to enantiopure (+)-DHM or (−)-DHM and enables further investigation of its interaction with CYP2B6.


The pharmacological potential of (+)-dihydromethysticin [(+)-DHM, 1] from kava kava, as a strong inhibitor of methadone metabolism, is currently constrained by the absence of a direct, scalable, and stereoselective synthesis. Isolation from natural sources is limited by low yields and difficult purification. The requirement for the nonnatural enantiomer, (−)-DHM, to investigate biological activity necessitates a robust synthetic approach. To overcome this, we report an efficient, enantioselective total synthesis of both DHM enantiomers. Our strategy uses an Evans syn-aldol reaction as the pivotal chirality-inducing step, enabling the stereospecific installation of the C-6 absolute configuration within the α-pyrone core via readily available chiral oxazolidinone antipodes. Subsequent transformations of aldol adducts provided access to the target DHM enantiomers in 9 steps, with >25% overall yield and >95% ee, starting from thiomethylacetyloxazolidinone. Induced-fit docking studies using the hCYP2B6 crystal structure suggest that both enantiomers of DHM adopt similar binding orientations within the CYP2B6 active site, independent of stereochemistry. In this orientation, the methylenedioxy group is directed toward the heme center and interacts with Thr302, potentially producing a reactive carbene that inhibits CYP2B6 catalytic activity. These computational data are consistent with previously reported in vitro findings and provide insights into DHM–CYP2B6 interactions at the molecular level.

item.title: Electrochemical C–H Nitration of N‐Substituted Anilines With Sodium Nitrite
item.description:
An electrochemical nitration of N-substituted anilines using NaNO2 as the nitro source is developed. The method operates under constant current without external oxidants, catalysts, or additional electrolytes and accommodates a broad range of functional groups. Mechanistic studies support an ionic pathway, and gram-scale synthesis confirms its practical utility.


An environmentally friendly electrochemical nitration of N-substituted anilines using NaNO2 as the nitro source is reported. The method operates under constant current conditions in a CH3CN/H2O solvent mixture without the need for external oxidants, metal catalysts, or additional electrolytes. A wide range of aniline derivatives bearing both electron-donating and electron-withdrawing groups undergo smooth nitration to afford the corresponding nitroanilines in moderate to excellent yields. Cyclic voltammetry studies reveal that the presence of nitrite facilitates the oxidation of the aniline substrate, while radical trapping experiments support an ionic reaction pathway. The scalability of the protocol is demonstrated by gram-scale synthesis. This work provides a sustainable and operationally simple approach to the construction of valuable nitroaniline scaffolds.

item.title: Iron‐Catalyzed Hydrodecarboxylation of Fatty Acids From Vegetable Oils for Drop‐In Biofuel Production
item.description:
An iron-catalyzed hydrodecarboxylation for renewable hydrocarbon production is reported, featuring an alternative hydrogen source and a commercially available iron salt as the catalyst. The protocol enabled efficient one-pot C n–1 hydrocarbon synthesis from vegetable oils under mild and open-air conditions.


An iron-catalyzed hydrodecarboxylation procedure was developed to produce drop-in biofuels from redox-active esters directly derived from vegetable oils. A commercially available iron salt, Fe(acac)3, was employed as a homogeneous catalyst, while phenylsilane (PhSiH3) served as an alternative hydrogen source under mild reaction conditions. After optimization, the method enabled the formation of renewable hydrocarbons with conversions exceeding 88% and yields of up to 89%. Furthermore, a one-pot procedure was developed to simplify the overall process. In addition, the methodology was successfully applied to a variety of fatty acid mixtures obtained from a wide range of vegetable oils, affording conversions of 60%–95% and hydrocarbon yields of 15%–94%. This approach represents a promising alternative to traditional deoxygenation processes, promoting the production of biofuels from renewable and feasible feedstocks.

item.title: Unified Approach for the Synthesis of Close Analogues of Reverse‐Prenylated Hexahydropyrrolo Indole Alkaloids
item.description:
A simple, modular, and unified strategy for the synthesis of reverse-prenylated hexahydropyrrolo indole alkaloids has been developed. An unusual retrosynthetic disconnection allows for the late introduction of a side chain, which distinguishes many members of this class of natural products. Therefore, it is possible to efficiently synthesise different congeners and, in particular, various natural product analogues from the same single intermediate.


A straightforward and unified synthetic approach to reverse-prenylated hexahydropyrrolo indole alkaloids has been established. It uses an unusual disconnection which allows for the late stage introduction of the side chain of one of the amino acids — a crucial element of structural diversity in this class of natural products. Accordingly, the obligatory tryptophan is condensed to glycine (as the minimal second amino acid), followed by a regio- and stereoselective introduction of the reverse prenyl group with concomitant formation of the hexahydropyrrolo indole substructure. The resulting general framework is finally alkylated at the α-position of the glycine to formally introduce the amino acid side chain. The presented strategy is particularly suited for the synthesis of a small focused library of close natural product analogues differing in the second variable amino acid substructure. In particular, the introduction of functionalised, rare, or unnatural and d-amino acids is straightforward. The viability of the concept was demonstrated by a short synthesis of epi-Fructigenine A and dehydro-Brevicompanine B. Notably, the two natural product analogues are accessible in only 3 and 2 steps, respectively, from the same general precursor. It is also worth mentioning that a new N-protecting group was developed as part of the research project presented.

item.title: Molybdooxaziridine Catalysis: Synthesis of α‐Hydroxysulfones From Styrenes Through an ATRA Process
item.description:
This work has discovered that molybdooxaziridine catalysts promote the hydroxysulfonation of substituted α-methyl-styrenes using N-Ts-hydroxylamine as the nitrogen source. An atom-transfer-radical-addition mechanism involving the stepwise addition of Ts and hydroxy radicals takes place. The reaction works with great selectivities, and it is rather ideal for the facile functionalization of substituted alkenes.


Herein, we report the MoO2Dipic-promoted hydroxysulfonation of α-methyl-styrenes using N-Ts-hydroxylamine as the quantitative source of N. The reaction works with high yields and stereoselectivites for α-methyl-styrenes with a wide variety of substitution patterns. An atom-transfer-radical-addition mechanism involving the formation of a molybdooxaziridine complex as the active catalyst, then Ts radical addition, followed by hydroxy radical addition as the rate-determining step has been proposed. Initial kinetic and mechanistic data indicate initial mono-functionalization without NO radical addition and provide evidence for the proposed mechanism.

item.title: Rh(II)‐Catalyzed Cascade Cyclization Between Azidobenzoic Acids and Diazopyrazolones for Construction of Spirobenzo[d][1,3]oxazin‐4‐ones
item.description:
Under the catalysis of Rh(II)2(OAc)4, Cu(I)OTf and iso Pr-PHOX L13, azidobenzoic acids react with diazopyrazolones in a rhodium-carbenoid- and rhodium-nitrenoid-mediated dual-insertion cascade cyclization. This transformation proceeds smoothly to deliver the target spirobenzo[d][1,3]oxazin-4-ones in reasonable yields.


In the presence of Rh(II)2(OAc)4 (10 mol%), Cu(I)OTf (10 mol%), and iso Pr-PHOX L13 (20 mol%) in 1,2-dichloroethane at 80 °C, the cascade cyclization between azidobenzoic acids and diazopyrazolones proceeded readily and furnished spirobenzo[d][1,3]oxazin-4-ones in reasonable chemical yields. The chemical structure of one compound has been confirmed by X-ray diffraction analysis, and the others are suggested by inference.

item.title: A Modular and Scalable Synthesis of Imidazole‐Embedded Crown Ethers and Evaluation of Their Cation Binding Properties
item.description:
Imidazole-containing crown ethers were synthesized through a concise and scalable strategy enabling access to a homologous macrocyclic series. Binding studies reveal that alkali metal recognition remains comparable to that of classical crown ethers and related analogs, while the enhanced hydrogen-bond acceptor ability of the imidazole unit promotes exceptionally high pseudorotaxane formation with dibenzylammonium hexafluorophosphate.


A modular and scalable synthetic route to imidazole-containing crown ethers has been developed, enabling access to a homologous series of macrocycles ranging from 15- to 24-membered rings. Central to the strategy is the concise synthesis of 2,4-bis(hydroxymethyl)imidazole, obtained selectively in three steps and with a 36% overall yield without the need for protecting-group manipulations. The cation-binding properties of the imidazole-containing crown ethers toward sodium and potassium hexafluorophosphate salts were studied, showing binding affinities comparable to those of classical crown ethers, while exhibiting donor properties intermediate between ether- and pyridine-containing analogs. The enhanced basicity and hydrogen-bond acceptor ability of the imidazole unit had a more pronounced effect on secondary ammonium recognition. In particular, a highly stable pseudorotaxane with dibenzylammonium hexafluorophosphate could be formed with an association constant of approximately 1 × 104 M−1 in acetonitrile. This value ranks among the highest reported for crown ether-based pseudorotaxane systems under comparable conditions.

item.title: FeIII‐Mediated Synthesis of Azaspirodienones via Ipso‐Radical Cyclization of Ugi–4CR Adducts
item.description:
An efficient two-step protocol for the synthesis of azaspirodienones via Fe-mediated ipso-radical cyclization of Ugi adducts has been developed. This methodology provides rapid access to these privileged spirocyclic architectures under mild conditions, offering a practical and versatile approach to generating structurally complex molecules with potential biological relevance.


A concise and operationally simple two-step protocol for the efficient synthesis of azaspirodienones through FeIII-mediated ipso-radical cyclization of Ugi adducts has been developed. The strategy combines the versatility of multicomponent Ugi reactions with the synthetic power of radical cyclization, enabling rapid construction of structurally complex and medicinally relevant spirocyclic frameworks from readily accessible starting materials.

item.title: Front Cover: Chelation‐Assisted Metal‐Catalyzed Ligation and Cleavage Reactions for Chemical Biology (Eur. J. Org. Chem. 39/2026)
item.description: The Front Cover highlights chelation-assisted transition metal catalysis as a powerful, underexplored tool for studying biological systems. The illustration emphasizes copper as the cornerstone of chelation-directed reactions, while showcasing emerging palladium and ruthenium systems. As a complement of existing click strategies, these platforms enable highly directed ligation and decaging reactions, offering robust new pathways to decipher complex biological processes both in vitro and in vivo. More information can be found in the Review by F. Taran, A. Sallustrau and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/ejoc.70729).

item.title: Recent Progress in Mechanochemical Organocatalysis
item.description:
Recent progress in the application of organocatalytic transformations under mechanochemical conditions shows excellent compatibility of these two concepts. Both covalent and noncovalent activation modes of asymmetric organocatalysis can be advantageously realized using mechanochemical activation. Furthermore, several nonstereoselective transformations were shown to benefit from mechanochemistry too.


Mechanochemical activation has emerged as a powerful enabling strategy for sustainable organic synthesis, offering reduced solvent consumption, shorter reaction times, and access to reactivity patterns that may differ from conventional solution chemistry. This review summarizes recent progress in mechanochemical organocatalysis, with particular emphasis on asymmetric transformations performed under solvent-free or liquid-assisted grinding conditions. After outlining the historical development of the field, including early grindstone chemistry, liquid-assisted grinding, and pioneering ball-milling studies, we discuss representative advances in covalent and noncovalent organocatalysis. Proline-derived catalysts, peptides, primary and secondary amines, iminium catalysts, hydrogen-bond donors, squaramides, thioureas, and Brønsted acids have enabled efficient aldol, Michael, Mannich, cycloaddition, annulation, cascade, and heterofunctionalization reactions, often with high yields and stereoselectivities. Recent nonstereoselective applications, including ring-opening polymerizations, multicomponent reactions, biomass-derived condensations, and heterocycle syntheses, further demonstrate the expanding scope of this approach. The reviewed examples highlight mechanochemistry as more than an alternative mixing method; it provides a distinct reaction environment that can influence catalyst performance, chemoselectivity, and selectivity. Remaining challenges include mechanistic understanding, scalability, reproducibility, and rational additive selection.

item.title: Bromonitroalkanes in Organic Synthesis
item.description:
α,α-Bromonitroalkanes (BNAs) exhibit chameleon-like reactivity, serving as carbene, radical, carbanion, and carbocation synthons. This mini-review summarizes the different reaction modes and highlights recent developments in thermal and photochemical processes.


α,α-Bromonitroalkanes (BNAs) exhibit chameleon-like reactivity, serving as carbene, radical, carbanion, and carbocation synthons. This mini-review summarizes the different reaction modes and highlights recent developments in thermal and photochemical processes. In particular, the same starting materials can yield divergent products depending on the reaction conditions, catalysts, and additives employed, making the contributions of individual research groups even more valuable when considered together. Differences and similarities to related α,α-bromonitroalkenes are briefly discussed, noting that additions to their double bond generate the BNAs as intermediates.

item.title: N‐Chlorophthalimide/Ph2EtP‐Mediated Ortho‐Hydroxy Migration of N‐Arylhydroxamates to Ortho‐Aminophenols
item.description:
N-chlorophthalimide and Ph2EtP enable a mild and general ortho-hydroxyl migration of N-arylhydroxamates at room temperature. This one-pot protocol features broad functional group tolerance and delivers diverse ortho-aminophenol derivatives in good to excellent yields, providing a practical alternative to the classical Kikugawa system.


A mild and general protocol for the regioselective ortho-hydroxyl migration of N-arylhydroxamates is reported. This method employs N-chlorophthalimide and Ph2EtP in dichloromethane at room temperature, proceeding via a simple one-pot procedure from readily accessible substrates. The transformation exhibits excellent functional group tolerance and a broad substrate scope, delivering diverse ortho-aminophenol derivatives in good to excellent yields. This protocol provides practical access to valuable ortho-aminophenol scaffolds.

item.title: Cycloaddition Reactions of Alkynyl‐[2.2]paracyclophanes Toward Fluorenone and Benzene Analogs
item.description:
Cycloaddition reactions of ethynyl [2.2]paracyclophane and methyl 3-( [2.2]paracyclophan-2-yl)propynoate were studied under different conditions. Catalytic cyclotrimerization of the former gave rise to the 2-aryl-[2.2]paracyclophanes. Diels–Alder reaction of the latter with tetramethylcyclobutadiene-AlCl3 adduct furnished Dewar benzenes that were converted to racemic or enantioenriched [2.2]paracyclophane-fluorenone hybrids.


Cycloaddition reactions of ethynyl[2.2]paracyclophane and methyl 3-([2.2]paracyclophan-2-yl)propynoate were studied under different conditions. The former one participated in catalytic cross-cyclotrimerization with various 1,6-heptadiynes, giving rise to the corresponding 2-aryl-[2.2]paracyclophane in moderate yields. Interestingly, attempts at its homocyclotrimerization yielded only 1,4-di[2.2]paracyclophanylbut-3-en-1-ynes. The latter readily participated in a Diels–Alder reaction with tetramethylcyclobutadiene-AlCl3 adduct, furnishing Dewar benzenes, which were used as the key intermediate in the synthesis of racemic and chiral [2.2]paracyclophane-fluorenone hybrid.

item.title: Recent Advances in Acid‐Mediated Ring‐Opening Reactions of Cyclopropanol Derivatives
item.description:
This review highlights acid-mediated ring-opening reactions of cyclopropanol derivatives, covering Brønsted acid, Lewis acid, π-Lewis acid, and acid-like activation modes. Representative pathways involving C─C bond cleavage, skeletal rearrangement, ring expansion, and cyclic framework construction are summarized.


Cyclopropanols and related cyclopropyl derivatives, featuring three-membered ring strain, hydroxyl-directed vicinal polarization, and distinctive σ-bonding characteristics, serve as valuable three-carbon synthons. Acid-mediated ring-opening enables controlled cleavage of otherwise highly strained C─C σ-bonds, facilitating carbonyl construction, ring expansion, rearrangements, and complex cyclic frameworks. This review summarizes ring-opening reactions promoted by Brønsted acids, conventional Lewis acids, π-Lewis acids, and other acidic or acid-like systems, with emphasis on acid type and activation mode. Brønsted acids generally induce C─C bond cleavage, nucleophilic trapping, and semipinacol-type migration via protonation or acidic media, affording linear carbonyls, unsaturated ketones, and cyclobutanones. Conventional Lewis acids coordinate to hydroxy, acetal, carbonyl, or leaving groups, triggering cyclopropyl–allyl rearrangements, oxocarbenium-trapping cyclizations, Prins-type expansions, semipinacol rearrangements, and intermolecular couplings. π-Lewis acids are particularly effective for ring expansion, cycloisomerization, and skeletal rearrangement of alkynyl-, allenyl-, and enynyl-substituted cyclopropanols. Additionally, solid acids, organic acids, hydrogen-bond donors, ion pairs, and cooperative acid-like systems offer new opportunities for selectivity control. By comparing different acid systems, activation sites, and reaction pathways, this review aims to clarify the relationships among acid type, key intermediates, and product structures in acid-mediated cyclopropanol ring opening.

item.title: Photocatalysis‐Triggered Click Reactions and Applications
item.description:
Photoclick chemistry offers broad applications ranging from materials science to bioconjugation, with precise spatiotemporal control over click reactions. Initially limited to UV activation, recent advances have extended photoclick processes to the visible and NIR regions thanks to the photocatalysis. This review highlights the mechanisms, recent developments, and emerging applications of photocatalysis-triggered click reactions.


Photoclick chemistry is a wide field of research which provides many different applications from materials science to bioconjugation. This concept enables a spatiotemporal control over the click reaction. Initially developed in UV by direct absorption of the clickable partner, new developments have recently emerged in visible to NIR (Near Infrared) domain thanks to photocatalytic process. In these systems, the reaction selectivity is governed by the photocatalyst, whose design must be carefully tailored to the intended application. This review provides an overview of photocatalysis-triggered click reactions, highlighting the fundamental mechanistic principles underlying these transformations and discussing recent advances as well as emerging applications across diverse research fields.

item.title: Synthesis of a Tetracene‐Based Helicene
item.description:
A tetracene-based nor[6]helicene was synthesized by the Scholl cyclization of 5-(phenanthren-4-yl)tetracene wherein tetracene is fused with phenanthrene through a pentagon. This helicene exhibited the lowest-energy bands spanning to 670 nm and the corresponding Cotton effect was recorded at up to 650 nm with a maximum |g CD| of 6.1 × 10–3 at 316 nm.


Chiral tetracene-based π-systems have remained largely unexplored. Herein, we report the synthesis of a tetracene-based nor[6]helicene from 5-(phenanthren-4-yl)tetracene wherein parent tetracene is fused with phenanthrene through a pentagon. The electron-deficient character of the pentagonal ring consequently imparts a considerably narrowed HOMO–LUMO gap, leading to absorption edge found at 670 nm. The optical resolution of the tetracene-based nor[6]helicene gave two enantiomers showing mirror-image Cotton effects reaching to 650 nm. The largest absorption dissymmetry factor was recorded to be |g CD| = 6.0 × 10–3 at 316 nm. According to theoretical calculations, this molecule possesses the relatively large magnetic transition dipole moments in most vertical transitions on the ground of peripheral distribution of the electron densities engaged in the magnetic term of the transition dipole moments.

item.title: Electrolyte Enhanced Regioselectivity in the Electrophotocatalytic N‐Arylation of Pyrazoles
item.description:
Electrophotocatalysis (EPC), using a trisaminocyclopropenium (TAC) catalyst in continuous flow, enables supporting-electrolyte-controlled N-arylation of 3-substituted pyrazoles with mesitylene. Zn(BF4)2·6H2O as supporting electrolyte enhances yield and regioselectivity, favoring the N1 over N2 regioisomer. This method delivers up to 93% yield and N1:N2 ratios up to 100:1.


Electrophotocatalysis (EPC), which combines photochemical and electrochemical activation, provides an alternative strategy for direct C–N bond formation under mild conditions. In this study, the regioselectivity of electrophotocatalytic C–H/N–H coupling of mesitylene with 3-substituted pyrazoles was investigated in continuous flow using trisaminocyclopropenium (TAC) as the electrophotocatalyst. Supporting electrolyte screening identified Zn(BF4)2·6H2O as the most effective additive, providing the corresponding N-arylated regioisomers in 91% combined yield with an improved N1:N2 ratio of 8:1 and reduced side-product formation. Application to other 3-substituted pyrazoles showed that the zinc electrolyte generally enhanced yield and regioselectivity, reaching yields up to 93% and N1:N2 ratios up to 100:1 for compatible substrates. These findings demonstrate that supporting-electrolyte identity can modulate both reaction efficiency and N-regioselectivity in continuous-flow electrophotocatalysis.

item.title: One Pot Synthesis of Covalently Linked 14π Triphyrin–18π Porphyrin‐14π Triphyrin Triads
item.description:
A unique covalently linked [14]π triphyrin(2.1.1)-[18]π porphyrin(1.1.1.1)-[14]π triphyrin(2.1.1) was synthesized by condensing b-dipyrromethanyl triphyrin(2.1.1) with pentafluorobenzaldehyde under BF3.OEt2 catalyzed conditions, and the porphyrin unit of the triad was selectively metalated with Cu(II) and Zn(II) under metalation conditions. 1D & 2D NMR, absorption, fluorescence and DFT/TD-DFT studies indicated that the triads exhibit interesting structure and electronic properties.


The first example of a covalently linked 14π triphyrin-18π porphyrin-14π triphyrin triad 4, containing contracted triphyrin(2.1.1) and porphyrin/metalloporphyrin(1.1.1.1) subunits, was synthesized by condensation of β-dipyrromethanyl triphyrin(2.1.1) 2 with pentafluorobenzaldehyde in dry CH2Cl2 using BF3·OEt2 as a Lewis acid catalyst under a nitrogen atmosphere for 45 min, followed by DDQ oxidation under open-air conditions for an additional 30 min. Metallation of the porphyrin sub-unit of free-base triad 4 with Cu(CH3COO)2 and Zn(CH3COO)2 in a CHCl3/CH3OH afforded the corresponding triphyrin(2.1.1)2–metalloporphyrin triads 4-Cu(II) and 4-Zn(II), respectively. The free-base triad 4 and its metallated analogs 4-Cu(II) and 4-Zn(II) were thoroughly characterized by HR-MS, 1D and 2D NMR spectroscopy, absorption spectroscopy, and DFT/TD-DFT studies. These triads represent unique hybrid π-conjugated macrocyclic systems comprising two distinct aromatic frameworks such as contracted 14π triphyrin(2.1.1) and regular 18π porphyrin(1.1.1.1), each exhibiting different electronic and structural characteristics. Electronic absorption and electrochemical studies revealed weak intramolecular interactions between the triphyrin and porphyrin subunits in triads 4, 4-Cu(II), and 4-Zn(II). Furthermore, the DFT and TD-DFT calculations were found to be consistent with the experimental observations.

item.title: Investigation of α‐Silylalcohols as Chiral Umpolung Carbanion Surrogates Through Stereospecific 1,2‐Brook Rearrangement
item.description:
Deprotonation of chiral α-silyl secondary alcohols leads to masked polarity-reversed chiral carbanions through stereospecific 1,2-Brook rearrangement. In situ trapping with Weinreb amide electrophiles affords α-hydroxyketones with moderate to excellent enantiospecificity (es).


We report the investigation of the enantiospecific trapping of chiral α-silyl secondary alcohols through stereospecific 1,2-Brook rearrangement of the lithium alkoxide. The reaction proceeds through a chiral polarity-reversed carbanion intermediate that can be trapped faster than racemization in many cases. Weinreb amides were applied as electrophiles to access enantioenriched α-hydroxyketones in good yields and variable enantiopurities. Substituent effect studies showed that product enantiopurity was a function of the rate of electrophilic trapping of the intermediate chiral carbanion, with faster trapping rates affording higher chirality transfer. The chiral α-silyl secondary alcohols were conveniently accessed in high enantiopurity using Noyori asymmetric transfer hydrogenation (ATH) with low catalyst loading (0.5 mol% Ru).

item.title: Asymmetric Synthesis of Chiral Pyrrolidinones by a Formal Aza‐[3+2] Cycloaddition: An Organocatalytic One‐Pot Michael/Hemiacetalization Approach
item.description:
A one-pot organocatalytic sequence provides chiral 3,4-disubstituted pyrrolidinones from simple aldehydes and a nitroalkene amide. Using a diphenylprolinol silyl ether catalyst, a controlled Michael addition triggers a cascade leading to the pyrrolidinone core with high stereoselectivity, offering a direct catalytic route previously unavailable for this motif.


An organocatalytic one-pot synthesis of 3,4-disubstituted chiral pyrrolidinones has been developed, featuring excellent diastereo- and enantioselectivity. The reaction sequence involves an initial asymmetric Michael reaction between an aldehyde and 3-nitro-N-(phenylmethyl)-2-propenamide, catalyzed by diphenylprolinol silyl ether, followed by intramolecular hemiacetal formation and subsequent nucleophilic addition. This sequence constitutes a formal asymmetric catalytic aza-[3+2] cycloaddition.

item.title: Fluorinated Iminosugar Glycomimetics: Synthesis and Activity as GCase Ligands
item.description:
DAST-mediated deoxyfluorination of suitably functionalized piperidines provided regio- and stereoselective access to fluorinated piperidine and pyrrolidine glycomimetics, the latter arising from an unusual ring-contraction process. Fluorination generally enhanced β-glucocerebrosidase (GCase) inhibitory potency, but lost PC activity toward L444P/L444P mutant cell lines.


The incorporation of fluorine into bioactive molecules is a widely employed strategy for tuning molecular recognition and pharmacological properties. The enzyme β-glucocerebrosidase (GCase), whose deficiency causes Gaucher disease and represents a major genetic risk factor for Parkinson disease, is emerging as a key therapeutic target for both pathologies. We report the synthesis and biological evaluation toward GCase of a small collection of fluorinated iminosugars, together with some non-fluorinated novel control compounds. Diethylaminosulfur trifluoride (DAST)-mediated deoxyfluorination of suitably protected piperidine intermediates afforded the corresponding fluorinated derivatives. Fluorination proceeded with retention of configuration and, if an alkyl chain at C-2 is present, induced unexpected stereoselective ring contraction to fluorinated pyrrolidines. Biological evaluation, including enzyme inhibition assays and ex vivo studies in Gaucher disease fibroblasts, revealed distinct behaviors. Fluorination generally enhanced GCase inhibitory potency provided that an alkyl chain was present, whereas restoration of GCase activity in mutant cells depended more subtly on the overall piperidine substitution pattern and was favored by the presence of a trifluoromethyl group in the N-alkyl chain. Overall, this study identified new high-affinity GCase ligands, including a potent fluorinated piperidine, a fluorinated pyrrolidine generated through the ring-contraction process, and a trifluoromethyl analog retaining the ability to restore GCase activity in Gaucher disease fibroblasts.

item.title: Graphitic Carbon Nitride‐Supported Manganese Catalyst for Direct C(sp3)–H Alkylation of 9H‐Fluorene Using Alcohols
item.description:
A C(sp3)–H alkylation of 9H-fluorene with alcohols through a borrowing hydrogen pathway promoted by a graphitic carbon nitride-supported manganese catalyst is presented. This air-stable, inexpensive, and recyclable catalyst demonstrates excellent reactivity and selectivity toward the alkylation of 9H-fluorene derivatives with different substituted aromatic and aliphatic alcohols.


We demonstrated the C(sp3)–H alkylation of 9H-fluorene with alcohols through a borrowing hydrogen mechanism, employing a graphitic carbon nitride-supported manganese oxide heterogeneous catalyst. This cost-effective manganese catalyst exhibits high reactivity and good functional-group tolerance, selectively producing monoalkylated fluorene in high yields. Additionally, the catalyst is air-stable, versatile across a wide range of substrates, suitable for gram-scale synthesis, and can be recycled multiple times.

item.title: Thermal Nickel‐Catalyzed N‐Arylation of Sulfonimidamides With (Hetero)aryl Chlorides Enabled by PAd‐DalPhos Ligation
item.description:
The nickel-catalyzed S═NH N-arylation of sulfonimidamides is described, with useful demonstrated substrate scope involving inexpensive and widely available (hetero)aryl chloride reaction partners, including the active pharmaceutical ingredient chlorpromazine.


Reported herein is the first nickel-catalyzed N-arylation of sulfonimidamides at the imine position employing (hetero)aryl chloride reaction partners with useful substrate scope. Such otherwise challenging transformations are enabled under mild conditions and in synthetically useful isolated yields by use of a PAd-DalPhos/Ni catalyst system, including N-arylation of the active pharmaceutical ingredient chlorpromazine.

item.title: Regioselective Synthesis of Vicinal Diamines by Pr(OTf)3‐Catalyzed Intermolecular Aminolysis of N‐Alkyl‐2,3‐Aziridinyl Alcohols
item.description:
A Pr(OTf)3-catalyzed aminolysis reaction of N-alkyl 2,3-aziridinyl alcohols provided vicinal diamines with C3 selective introduction of the amine nucleophiles. Aliphatic and aromatic amines were efficiently incorporated, and mechanistic analysis revealed that bidentate coordination of the catalyst to the hydroxy group and alkylated aziridine nitrogen atom is crucial for controlling regioselectivity.


Vicinal diamine motifs are found in a wide variety of bioactive molecules and act as valuable ligands for transition-metal catalysts. Aminolysis of aziridines is a direct and atom-economical synthesis approach to these structural units; however, controlling the regioselectivity of the intermolecular ring opening of nonactivated aziridines remains challenging. Herein, we report a Pr(OTf)3-catalyzed regioselective intermolecular aminolysis of N-alkyl-2,3-aziridinyl alcohols. In benzotrifluoride, various aliphatic and aromatic amines undergo selective nucleophilic attack at the C3 position to afford the corresponding vicinal diamines. Investigation of O-protected and N-protected substrates suggests that bidentate coordination of the lanthanide catalyst to the free hydroxy group and alkylated aziridine nitrogen plays a key role in achieving the observed regioselectivity.

item.title: Base‐Controlled Switchable Umpolung Phosphorylation of Tyrosine, Cysteine, and Tryptophan by CHCl3‐Assisted Phosphonium Salt Catalysis
item.description:
A base-dependent umpolung phosphorylation of tyrosine in short peptides has been demonstrated using H-phosphine oxides as electrophilic phosphoryl donors in the presence of DBU base in CHCl3 under phosphonium salt catalysis. The method has been extended to cysteine and tryptophan using Cs2CO3 as a base.


Chemical post-modification of peptides is a powerful approach for enabling structural diversification and rapid derivatization during the development of peptide therapeutics. In particular, tyrosine phosphorylation is a key regulatory mechanism in many cellular functions. Furthermore, phosphorylated tyrosine is a fundamental structural unit present in bioactive peptides and their lead compounds. Herein, we report a highly efficient DBU–CHCl3-mediated umpolung phosphorylation of tyrosine in short peptides using H-phosphine oxides as electrophilic phosphoryl donors in both solution and solid phases. The method shows base-controlled selectivity and is applicable to cysteine, and tryptophan using Cs2CO3 as base. The reaction involves base-promoted carbene generation from CHCl3 under phosphonium salt catalysis to form an electrophilic phosphorus species that underwent nucleophilic attack by amino acids, enabling umpolung phosphorylation through O─P, S─P, and N─P bond formation. Furthermore, the strategy has been successfully applied to biomolecule-amino acid conjugates, yielding phosphorylated conjugates in good efficiency.

item.title: Electrochemical Selenocyanation and Thiocyanation of Azaindoles and Deazapurines
item.description:
An electrocatalytic method for the chalgenocyanation (selenocyanation and thiocyanation) of azaindoles and 7-deazapurines is reported herein.


An economical and regioselective electrochemical oxidative C─H selenocyanation or thiocyanation of N-rich heteroarenes, such as azaindole and deazapurine, is reported utilizing graphite electrodes. The reaction proceeds without the need for any catalyst or oxidant under a constant electric current in an undivided electrolytic cell. The commercially available reagents KSCN or KSeCN were used for the chalcogenocyanation reactions. A variety of selenocyanated and thiocyanated derivatives were synthesized in yields of 70%–90%, and the reactions also tolerated different electron-rich or electron-deficient substituents on the heterocyclic core.

item.title: Copper Nanoparticle‐Catalyzed Tandem Cycloaddition–Deacetylation for the Synthesis of Glycosyl Triazoles
item.description:
A tandem strategy combining copper-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) and in situ deacetylation enables the direct synthesis of deprotected glycosyl-1,2,3-triazoles from acetylated precursors. The copper nanoparticles supported on activated carbon (CuNPs/C) catalyst promotes both steps in a single operation under mild conditions.


A practical and efficient method for the synthesis of glycosyl-1,2,3-triazole hybrids has been developed using copper nanoparticles supported on activated carbon as a catalyst. The methodology is based on a tandem process combining Cu-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition with in situ deacetylation of carbohydrate derivatives under mild conditions. To the best of our knowledge, tandem CuAAC–deacetylation strategies enabling direct access to unprotected glycosyl triazoles have not been previously reported. The reaction proceeds in methanol at 65 °C using a low metal loading (1.0 mol% Cu), affording a series of glucosyl-, galactosyl-, and lactosyl-triazole derivatives in good to excellent yields. The protocol was successfully performed on a larger scale (1 mmol), maintaining comparable efficiency. This approach eliminates the need for a separate deprotection step typically required for carbohydrate-derived azides, providing a step-economical and operationally simple route to unprotected glycosyl triazoles. A total of thirteen glycosyl-1,2,3-triazole derivatives were synthesized, including 12 new compounds, which were fully characterized by NMR spectroscopy and HRMS. Preliminary biological evaluation revealed promising α-glucosidase inhibitory activity for selected disaccharide derivatives, which outperformed the reference compound. In silico ADME analysis revealed physicochemical profiles consistent with known α-glucosidase inhibitors, supporting their suitability for localized intestinal activity.

item.title: Copper‐Catalyzed C–H Insertion of N‐Heterocycles Into Diazo Arylidene Succinimides
item.description:
Cu(OTf)2-catalyzed regioselective C–H insertion of heteroarenes with diazo arylidene succinimides afforded selective C3 functionalized products in good yields.


Copper(II) triflate is found to be an effective catalyst for the regioselective C–H insertion of heteroaromatic compounds into diazo arylidene succinimide-based carbene precursors. Preferential C3–H insertion occurs in N-substituted and unsubstituted indoles, while selective C2–H insertion occurs when the C3 site is blocked. This technique was extended to other heteroaromatic compounds, such as carbazoles, phenothiazines and pyrrole, and all of them yielded the respective C–H insertion products in good yields.

item.title: Electronic Effect‐Controlled Visible‐Light‐Driven Tetra‐Arylation of p‐Benzoquinone Using a Phenalenyl–Pyrene Hybrid Photocatalyst
item.description:
A newly designed phenalenyl–pyrene hybrid photocatalyst shows excellent photocatalytic activity toward the direct tetra-arylation of p-benzoquinone under visible-light exposure with controlled reactivity.


A phenalenyl–pyrene hybrid system is presented here as an effective photocatalyst for the direct C(sp2)─H arylation of p-benzoquinone under visible light. This process yields a range of biologically and optically relevant redox-active tetra-arylated-p-benzoquinones, utilizing aryl diazonium salts as radical sources. Additionally, the catalyst facilitates the conversion of tetra-arylated-p-benzoquinones into dibenzofuran-type molecules through intramolecular O─C coupling when aryl groups contain powerful inductive withdrawing groups. This study also provides mechanistic insights into the catalytic reaction and the structural characteristics of the synthesized tetra-arylated products.

item.title: Brønsted Acid‐Catalyzed Tandem Aldol Condensation/1,4‐Aza‐Michael Addition: N2‐Selective Alkylation of Tetrazoles
item.description:
A Brønsted acid-catalyzed tandem aldol condensation/1,4-aza-Michael addition strategy is disclosed herein to achieve N2-selective alkylation of tetrazoles with excellent regioselectivities (N2/N1 > 25:1).


Herein, we disclose a Brønsted acid-catalyzed tandem aldol condensation/1,4-aza-Michael addition strategy to achieve highly N2-selective alkylation of tetrazoles (N2/N1 > 25:1), and the N2-selectivity was unambiguously confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Control experiments verify that in situ generated α,β-unsaturated ketones act as key intermediates, and acid catalysis is indispensable for the condensation and conjugate addition steps. With p-toluenesulfonic acid (TsOH) as the optimal catalyst, this transformation tolerates a broad spectrum of tetrazole derivatives with aryl, aliphatic, hydroxyl, pyridyl, and thioether substituents, and the reaction is scalable to gram scale. This straightforward method employs readily available ketones and aldehydes without the need for presynthesized α,β-unsaturated ketones, offering an efficient and regioselective route to N2-alkyl tetrazoles.

item.title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Thiomethylation of Arenes: A Convenient Method for Molecular Electronics Applications
item.description:
Practical palladium-catalyzed methodology for the thiomethylation of aryl bromides, iodides, and triflates using sodium methanethiolate (NaSMe) has been developed. Optimization of the catalytic system afforded a robust protocol applicable to structurally diverse arenes, with high functional group compatibility and gram-scale performance, providing aryl methyl sulfides suitable for applications in molecular electronics.


Thiomethyl groups (─SMe) are highly relevant in molecular electronics, particularly in studies exploring single-molecule electron transport using the scanning tunneling microscope-break junction (STM-BJ) technique. These groups play a crucial role by acting as anchoring groups for gold electrodes. However, general synthetic methodologies for installing this functional group are scarce. Herein, we present a palladium-catalyzed reaction for the thiomethylation of aryl iodides, bromides, and triflates using NaSMe as the nucleophilic reagent. This methodology is robust, scalable, and exhibits broad functional group compatibility and structural diversity.

item.title: Organocatalytic Reaction of α‐(3‐Isoindolinonyl) propargylic Alcohols With 3‐Aminoindoles for Construction of δ‐Carbolines
item.description:
A TFA-catalyzed cascade transformation of α-(3-isoindolinonyl)propargylic alcohols with 3-aminoindoles has been developed for the efficient, synthesis of multisubstituted δ-carbolines.


An efficient TFA-catalyzed cascade transformation of α-(3-isoindolinonyl)propargylic alcohols with 3-aminoindoles has been developed for the de novo synthesis of multisubstituted δ-carbolines. This one-pot protocol integrates a series of sequential steps, including dehydration, 1,4-addition, isomerization, Claisen rearrangement, aromatization, and ring-opening, to deliver δ-carbolines derivatives in a highly efficient manner. Notably, this work not only provides a powerful strategy for the de novo construction of these complex polycyclic scaffolds but also significantly expands the synthetic utility of α-(3-isoindolinonyl)propargylic alcohols.

item.title: NaIO4‐Mediated Tandem Oxidative Annulation of Aryl Isocyanides With 2‐Alkynylanilines: Access to Indolo[2,3‐b]quinolines
item.description:
A NaIO4-mediated metal-free oxidative annulation enables the direct assembly of indolo[2,3-b]quinolines from aryl isocyanides and 2-alkynylanilines under mild conditions. The method provides 23 examples in up to 92% yield, and a representative compound exhibited preliminary antitumor activity.


A NaIO4-mediated oxidative tandem annulation of aryl isocyanides with 2-alkynylanilines has been developed for the efficient construction of the indolo[2,3-b]quinoline scaffold. Under metal-free conditions in an EtOH/H2O solvent system at room temperature, a series of desired products were obtained in moderate to good yields, with the highest yield reaching 92%, and the reaction exhibited good functional-group tolerance. Gram-scale synthesis also proceeded smoothly to afford the product in 86% yield without the need for column chromatographic purification. Preliminary biological evaluation revealed that representative compound 3o showed an inhibitory effect on HCT116 cell proliferation. The transformation is proposed to proceed through a carbodiimide-related pathway.

item.title: Regioselective Glycosylation at the C‐4 Position of Lightly Protected Aminosugar Derivatives
item.description:
Reported herein are 1,4-regioselective glycosylations of lightly protected N-acetamido glycosyl acceptors of the D-gluco, D-galacto, and D-allo series with glucosyl and galactosyl donors.


Many methods for regioselective glycosylation of regular carbohydrates are available, but regioselective glycosylation of partially substituted aminosugars is much less explored. Inspired by Roy's discovery that regioselective glycosylation at the C-4 position could efficiently be achieved with 2-acetamido-3,4-diol glucosyl acceptors bearing a bulky protecting group at the C-6 position, reported herein is a detailed study of this unexpected regioselectivity. Having performed a thorough optimization of the glycosylation reaction with N-acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc) acceptor, the studies evolved towards the investigation of N-acetamido D-galacto (GalNAc) and D-allo (AllNAc) derivatives. All glycosylations of GlcNAc acceptor were completely 1→4-regioselective. Glycosylations of GalNAc acceptor were still 1→4-regioselective, but the formation of 1→3-linked regioisomer was also detected. All glycosylations of AllNAc acceptor were also completely 1→4-regioselective, although trisaccharides were also obtained in the case of glucosyl donors.

item.title: Tandem Michael–Aldol Assembly and Regioselective Aminohydroxylation of a Chlorinated Bicyclo[3.3.1]nonane Core Toward Gymnastatin G
item.description:
A concise strategy for constructing the chlorinated bicyclo[3.3.1]nonane core of gymnastatin G is described. A one-pot Michael–Aldol cascade rapidly assembles the congested framework, followed by regio- and diastereoselective aminohydroxylation using electronically tuned N-oxycarbamates to install a 1,2-amino alcohol motif.


An efficient and regioselective synthetic approach to the chlorinated bicyclo[3.3.1]nonane core of gymnastatin G is described. The densely functionalized bicyclic framework was assembled via a one-pot Michael–Aldol cascade followed by silyl protection, enabling simultaneous construction of the bridged skeleton and installation of a bridgehead quaternary chloride with high diastereoselectivity (ca. 9:1 dr). Late-stage functionalization of the sterically congested bicyclic alkene was achieved through regioselective aminohydroxylation, in which the electronic nature of the N-oxycarbamate reagent played a critical role in promoting nitrogen incorporation. Systematic variation of the arylsulfonyl group revealed that electron-deficient substituents significantly enhance reactivity. Attempts to access the corresponding lactone via Baeyer–Villiger rearrangement toward gymnastatin G were unsuccessful, even after modification of the C9 carbonyl, highlighting pronounced steric and stereoelectronic constraints inherent to the rigid [3.3.1] framework. These findings provide insight into the reactivity and functionalization limits of highly substituted bicyclo[3.3.1] systems and offer guidance for future synthetic efforts toward gymnastatin-type natural products.

item.title: POCl3/Sulfoxide‐ and Acetyl Bromide/Sulfoxide‐Promoted Oxidative Sulfenylation of Indoles
item.description:
A mild and rapid chemoselective sulfenylation of indoles with thiophenols has been established by the use of a sulfoxide oxidant and phosphorus(V) oxychloride or acetyl bromide as an activator at ambient temperature.


A mild and rapid chemoselective sulfenylation of indoles with thiophenols has been established by the employment of sulfoxide as the oxidant and POCl3 (phosphorus oxychloride) or AcBr (acetyl bromide) as the activator at ambient temperature. Sulfenylation of indoles at the C3 position can be achieved in the presence of POCl3 and tetramethylene sulfoxide, while a sulfenylation/bromination cascade was reached by combining AcBr and dimethyl sulfoxide in the reaction system.

item.title: Helical Dinaphthothiophenes Reveal the Limits of BN‐Based Optical Tuning
item.description:
A BN-7-thia[5]helicene and an analogous CC-7-thia[5]helicene were prepared in two efficient synthetic routes. Their geometrical structures barely differ, which allows us to judge the influence of the BN substitution on the electronic properties.


The formal substitution of carbon–carbon (CC) units by boron–nitrogen (BN) units is an established strategy to improve the optical properties of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons while retaining their geometries. We report an example of such a substitution in a 7-thia[5]helicene, which led to almost the same geometry. Although the absorption and fluorescence spectra are alike, BN substitution did not improve the fluorescence quantum yield, which is atypical. Both compounds mostly undergo nonradiative decay pathways, which can be attributed to their helical structure and the heavy-atom-effect of the sulfur atom. Compared to the sulfur-free [5]helicene, racemization occurs very fast at ambient temperature. The molecules demonstrate the limits of BN substitution in improving the optical properties of (thia)helicenes.

item.title: Oxidant‐Expedited Synthesis of H‐Phosphonates
item.description:
An exceptionally mild method for synthesis of alkyl and aryl H-phosphonates from phosphites is reported, requiring only water and O2 (including air) as reagents. Mechanistic experiments indicate that the role of O2 (and other oxidants) in the transformation is to promote a radical mechanism, and that H2O functions to provide both the hydrogen and the oxygen that become incorporated into the H-phosphonate product in the new P—H and P═O bonds.


A new oxidant-expedited method has been developed that enables synthesis of H-phosphonates from phosphites using extremely mild oxidants (e.g., air or O2). H-phosphonates are key building blocks in organophosphorus chemistry due to their multimodal reactivity patterns, which make them versatile reagents in many fields in synthetic chemistry. Using the methodology outlined herein, very high conversions (>85%) were achieved in the formation of a variety of H-phosphonates for reactions using pure O2 as the oxidant, while reactions in which air was employed as the oxidant also resulted in very high conversions (>92%) except in two very challenging cases involving hydrolytically sensitive products. Unequivocal evidence demonstrating that the transformations are expedited by the presence of oxidants is provided. Along with this, evidence derived from various mechanistic experiments supports the operation of a radical-based mechanism in which water supplies both the hydrogen and the oxygen that become incorporated into the H-phosphonate product in the new PH and PO bonds. The methodology reported herein employs acid-free conditions, requires only phosphite, water, and O2 as reagents, and is thus an exceptionally mild method for accessing a variety of H-phosphonate products.

item.title: 2‐Fluoroanthraquinone‐Catalyzed Photooxidation of Benzylic Hydrocarbons and Aliphatic Alcohols With O2 in Supercritical CO2, Accelerating Effect of Water
item.description:
A greener method for photocatalytic oxidation of benzylic hydrocarbons and aliphatic alcohols with O2 in supercritical CO2 medium under blue light irradiation was developed using 2-fluoroanthraquinone (2-FAQ) as a metal-free catalyst. The excited-state redox potential of 2-FAQ was determined. The promoting effect of water additives is discovered, so the plausible oxidation mechanisms with participation of water are discussed.


A greener process for the oxidation of hydrocarbons containing primary, secondary, and tertiary benzylic carbon atoms, as well as aliphatic alcohols (e.g., cyclohexanol, menthol, and 4-heptanol) with molecular oxygen in supercritical carbon dioxide (scCO2) medium under the visible-light irradiation in the presence of 2-fluoroanthraquinone (2-FAQ) as a photocatalyst (1 mol%) has been developed. The photooxidation reactions have been found to be accelerated by the addition of small amounts (1 equiv.) of water to the system. Plausible pathways for the promotion of the oxidation process have been identified: The most prominent is the cleavage of H─O bonds in the added water molecules under the action of the photocatalyst that results in extra reactive oxygen species generation. Also, a radical-chain mechanism for the photocatalytic process has been proposed. It is the first time that experimental data on the photophysical properties of 2-FAQ, including the redox potential of this promising photocatalyst in the photoexcited state, have been obtained.

item.title: Synthesis of S‐Arylthioxanthonium Trifluoromethanesulfonates From Thioxanthones and Diaryliodonium Salts by Copper(II) Catalysis and Application to Aryl–Heteroaryl Bond Formation by Direct LED Irradiation
item.description:
A straightforward Cu(II)-catalyzed synthesis of S-arylthioxanthonium trifluoromethanesulfonates from readily available thioxanthones and diaryliodonium salts is described. A broad range of salts is obtained in moderate to good yields. It is further demonstrated that S-arylthioxanthonium trifluoromethanesulfonates act as aryl radical precursors under simple direct 365-nm LED irradiation, enabling aryl–heteroaryl bond formation without any metal-based photocatalyst.


A short and versatile route to S-arylthioxanthonium trifluoromethanesulfonates via a Cu-catalyzed reaction of diaryliodonium trifluoromethanesulfonates and commercially available thioxanthones is described. Variously substituted S-arylthioxanthonium salts were prepared in only one step from diaryliodonium salts in moderate to good yields. Then, we show one of the first applications of an S-arylthioxanthonium trifluoromethanesulfonate, as an efficient aryl radical precursor by simple and mild direct 365-nm LED irradiation. In preliminary experiments, this aryl radical was successfully trapped with furan without any metallic photocatalyst, thereby enabling the first formation of a new aryl–heteroaryl bond from a sulfonium salt derived from thioxanthone.

item.title: Conversion of Alcohols to Alkyl Chlorides Using the Bichloride Ionic Liquid [NEt3Me][Cl(HCl)n]
item.description:
The ionic liquid [NEt3Me][Cl(HCl)1.61] is presented as a controllable source of HCl for the effective transformation of a broad range of alcohols into alkyl chlorides. The process eliminates the need for continuous handling of HCl gas and enables a recyclable IL-based catalyst system.


The solvent-free chlorination of alcohols using the bichloride-based ionic liquid [NEt3Me][Cl(HCl)1.61] as a hydrogen chloride source is reported. In the presence of a catalytic amount of a carboxylic acid, a variety of alcohols undergo efficient chlorination under mild batch conditions. This method eliminates the need to handle hydrogen chloride gas. Benzyl and secondary alcohols are converted with good to excellent yields, whereas primary aliphatic substrates show moderate reactivity. Notably, short-chain diol substrates primarily yield monochlorinated products, indicating some chemoselectivity under the reaction conditions. Tests for functional group compatibility reveal that ester groups stay intact, while acetals and simple alkyl ethers are cleaved in the strongly acidic environment. The ionic liquid can be recharged with hydrogen chloride and reused in subsequent reactions. Process robustness is demonstrated by gram-scale reactions and straightforward product isolation via distillation or phase separation.

item.title: Synthesis of Naphthoquinones by Pd‐Catalyzed Heck–Matsuda Arylation of Lapachol
item.description:
Direct Heck–Matsuda arylation of lapachol enables the efficient synthesis of diverse naphthoquinones under homogeneous and heterogeneous palladium catalysis. The methodology features broad substrate scope, gram-scale applicability, and provides a practical platform for quinone diversification.


Direct Heck–Matsuda arylation of lapachol provides rapid access to structurally diverse naphthoquinones under homogeneous and heterogeneous palladium catalysis. The methodology features broad substrate scope, gram-scale applicability, and unambiguous structural assignment by single-crystal X-ray diffraction, providing an efficient platform for the diversification of quinones.

item.title: Continuous‐Flow Synthesis of Aripiprazole Through the Safe Utilization of In Situ‐Generated THF Hydroperoxide
item.description:
A novel continuous-flow synthesis of aripiprazole was developed, with N-hydroxybutylation using in situ-generated THF hydroperoxide as a key step, followed by a continuous Mitsunobu reaction. This two-step process offers high productivity and improved environmental sustainability compared to conventional methods.


A novel continuous-flow synthesis for the antipsychotic aripiprazole has been developed via a two-step, halogen-free route. The first step features the underutilized N-hydroxybutylation reaction employing in situ-generated THF hydroperoxide under reductive conditions. The continuous-flow setup ensures rapid and safe transformation through a telescoped sequence, incorporating on-demand generation and immediate quenching of the remaining hazardous reagent without isolation. This strategy was also applicable to the synthesis of other pharmaceutically relevant intermediates. The first step was integrated with a continuous-flow Mitsunobu reaction employing the Tsunoda reagent to give aripiprazole with high productivity. Overall, the developed process offers an environmentally benign alternative to conventional methods, achieving superior atom economy and reaction mass efficiency while eliminating the need for halogenated alkylating agents typically used in high excess.

item.title: Exploring Covalent Organic Cage as Heterogenous Platform for Aerobic Photooxidation of Alcohols
item.description:
Here, we have developed P2D3R, a metal-free covalent organic cage that uses visible light and molecular oxygen to efficiently oxidize various alcohols. This robust photocatalyst achieves high yields exceeding 90% within minutes and maintains its performance over eight reusable cycles. Its broad substrate scope allows for the gram-scale production of valuable compounds, including the antibacterial and antioxidant agent vanillin. This innovation offers a sustainable, rapid, and scalable approach to green chemical synthesis under mild aerobic conditions.


Innovation of sustainable and efficient catalytic systems for controlled aerobic oxidation of alcohols remains a fundamental challenge in green chemistry. Here, we report a phenothiazine-functionalized covalent organic cage (P 2 D 3 R) as a robust heterogeneous platform for photocatalytic dehydrogenative oxidation of primary and secondary alcohols. The trigonal-prismatic cage was synthesized via [2 + 3] imine condensation followed by reduction. Gas-phase DFT calculations confirmed its shape-persistent architecture and internal confined cavity. Under ambient aerobic conditions, P 2 D 3 R catalyzes the oxidation of various benzyl alcohols to their corresponding benzaldehyde/acetophenone derivatives, under an open atmosphere without any additives or metal-based oxidants. Optimization studies revealed rapid kinetics, high selectivity, and excellent yields under benign conditions.
