The catalysis demonstrates broad substrate scope for efficiently oxidizing aryl and heteroaryl alcohols bearing both electron-donating and electron-withdrawing substituents with high yields (>90%) and gram-scale scalability within minutes. Moreover, the catalyst is recoverable and reusable over eight cycles without loss of catalytic activity. Notably, two value-added natural products, vanillin and camphor, were obtained from this present catalysis, where vanillin is well known for its antibacterial and antioxidant properties. This work highlights organic cages as a promising porous material for next-generation additive-free photocatalysts, integrating light harvesting, substrate confinement, and recyclability within discrete multifunctional systems.

item.title: Copper‐Catalyzed Hydroxylation of Simple Fluoroaryl and Aryl Chlorides: A Route to (Fluoro)phenols
item.description:
A copper-catalyzed conversion of simple polyfluoroaryl chlorides to the corresponding phenols was developed. A simple ligand system was applied, as well as potassium carbonate as an inexpensive and effective base, while significantly suppressing competing SNAr pathways. Use of a sulfolane/water solvent system enabled high reactivity at a low catalyst loading, underscoring the practicality and scalability of this protocol.


A copper-catalyzed conversion of polyfluoroaryl chlorides to the corresponding phenols was developed. A simple ligand system was applied, as well as potassium carbonate as an inexpensive and effective base, while significantly suppressing competing SNAr pathways. The generality of the method was further demonstrated with simple aryl chlorides, which also underwent efficient hydroxylation. Mechanistic studies suggest that the reaction proceeds via a Cu(I)/Cu(III) catalytic cycle. Notably, the use of a sulfolane/water solvent system enabled high reactivity at a low catalyst loading, underscoring the practicality and scalability of this protocol.

item.title: Developing a p‐Toluenesulfonic Acid/Benzenesulfonic Acid/Water Mixture as Sustainable Medium for Aqueous Diels–Alder Reactions of Hydrophobic Anthracenes and Various Dienophiles
item.description:
Classic Diels–Alder reactions generally require anhydrous organic solvents, resulting in significant solvent waste. Herein, we established an aqueous Diels–Alder reaction by using acidic hydrotropes to generate a sustainable medium. The method features good functional group compatibility of various dienophiles and excellent solvent recyclability, providing various bridged cycloadducts in excellent yield.


Aqueous Diels–Alder reactions are highly attractive for green chemistry because of their 100% atom economy and solvent waste mitigation. Despite significant effort, reactions involving hydrophobic dienes and water-sensitive dienophiles, or vice versa, remain challenging. Herein, we implemented an efficient Diels–Alder reaction in a mixture of aqueous p-toluenesulfonic acid and benzenesulfonic acid as a recyclable medium. The methodology features good compatibility with hydrophobic anthracenes and water-sensitive dienophiles, excellent yields, and chromatography-free product isolation. The aqueous medium could easily be recovered and reused multiple times without additional processing.

item.title: Copper‐Catalyzed Synthesis of Benzimidazole‐Fused Phenanthridines and Quinolines
item.description:
Benzimidazole-fused phenanthridines and quinolines are constructed by copper-catalyzed C(sp2)─C and C(sp2)─N couplings between 2-(2-bromoaryl)benzimidazoles/2-(2-bromovinyl)benzimidazoles and 2-bromoarylboronic acids under microwave irradiation.


A modular synthetic method for benzimidazole-fused phenanthridines, benzo[4,5]imidazo[1,2-f]phenanthridines, has been developed via copper-catalyzed sequential C(sp2)─C and C(sp2)─N bond formations between 2-(2-bromoaryl)benzimidazoles and 2-bromoarylboronic acids under microwave irradiation. The construction of benzimidazole-fused quinolines, benzo[4,5]imidazo[1,2-a]quinolines, is also achieved by treating 2-(2-bromovinyl)benzimidazoles with 2-bromophenylboronic acid under similar copper catalysis. A control experiment indicates the involvement of competing copper-catalyzed Suzuki–Miyaura-type C─C and Ullmann-type C─N coupling pathways.

item.title: Sustainable Catalyst‐Free Synthesis of Substituted Pyrazoles Through an Annulation/Oxidation Cascade Under Batch and Continuous‐Flow Methods
item.description:
This method enables a sustainable, catalyst-free synthesis of highly functionalized pyrazoles via a formal [3 + 2] annulation-oxidation approach in batch and continuous-flow conditions.


We describe a catalyst-free synthesis of substituted pyrazoles in good to excellent yields using α,β-unsaturated β-ketoesters and aryl hydrazines under mild reaction conditions. The reaction proceeds through a Michael-initiated ring closure reaction followed by in situ oxidation. A broad range of substrates bearing electron-withdrawing and electron-donating substituents was successfully converted to the corresponding pyrazole derivatives. The method was scalable under batch conditions, demonstrating its practical applicability. In addition, the ester group present in the products could be transformed into the corresponding carboxylic acid and amide derivatives, providing access to structurally diverse pyrazole scaffolds. The protocol was also translated to continuous-flow conditions, offering an efficient and sustainable route to these valuable heterocyclic compounds.

item.title: Synthesis of β‐ and γ‐Carbolinones Through a Fe(III)‐Mediated Radical 6‐Endo‐Trig Cyclization of Indole‐Based Ugi 4‐CR Adducts
item.description:
A practical strategy for synthesizing β- and γ-carbolinones from indole-based Ugi 4-CR adducts through an intramolecular radical cyclization using Fe(III)–H species is presented. This approach enables the efficient synthesis of spiro-carbolinones under mild reaction conditions and demonstrates the effectiveness of secondary radicals in both cyclization pathways.


A novel protocol for Fe(III)-mediated 6-endo-trig radical cyclization of indole-based Ugi 4-CR adducts has been developed, facilitating the synthesis of β - and γ-carbolinones via the formation of Fe(III)–H as a key species. This atom-efficient approach proceeds under mild conditions and demonstrates broad functional group tolerance.

item.title: Synthesis of Cysteine–Fluorophore Conjugates by Visible‐Light‐Promoted Thiol–Ene Coupling Using Organic Photocatalysts
item.description:
Cysteine–fluorophore conjugates were efficiently prepared through a visible-light-driven thiol–ene approach employing solely organic photocatalysts. The reaction proceeds under mild, metal-free conditions. The fluorophore scope includes mono- and dialkene-functionalized naphthalene, naphthalimide, and aromatic diimide derivatives. Cysteine incorporation largely preserved the optical properties of the parent fluorophores.


In this work, we have investigated the visible-light-mediated thiol–ene coupling of N-acetyl-L-cysteine methyl ester with structurally distinct alkene-functionalized fluorophores using metal-free organic photocatalysts under mild conditions. The fluorophore set comprised naphthalene, naphthalimide, and aromatic diimide derivatives featuring different alkene environments and linker architectures. The transformations were promoted under mild and metal-free conditions using five organic photocatalysts belonging to three distinct structural families, namely acridinium salts, BOPHY derivatives, and xanthene dyes. The methodology proved to be compatible with structurally diverse fluorophore architectures and enabled the efficient preparation of both mono- and bis-functionalized cysteine conjugates. Reaction efficiency was influenced by fluorophore structure and photocatalyst identity, with yields reaching up to 95% for styrenyl naphthalimide derivatives. Sequential thiol–ene additions were successfully achieved for divinyl fluorophores, providing access to doubly functionalized products under the same reaction conditions. Photophysical studies demonstrated that cysteine incorporation generally preserves the absorption and emission characteristics of the parent fluorophores and, in several cases, leads to enhanced fluorescence quantum yields. These results establish visible-light-mediated thiol–ene coupling as a straightforward and versatile approach for the preparation of fluorescent cysteine building blocks from structurally diverse fluorophore scaffolds.

item.title: Piv2O‐Mediated Esterification of Carboxylic Acids With Phenols Enabled by NMI Catalysis
item.description:
A mild, stereoretentive Piv2O/NMI catalytic system for direct esterification of carboxylic acids with phenols is established. It features broad substrate compatibility, good enantiopurity retention, and simple postprocessing. Mechanistic studies confirm pivalate’s key role in phenol activation via N-acylimidazolium intermediates.


A green, stereoretentive esterification of carboxylic acids with phenols has been developed using N-methylimidazole (NMI) as the catalyst and pivalic anhydride (Piv2O) as the carboxylic acid activator. The reaction proceeds in ethyl acetate, exhibits broad functional group tolerance and minimal racemization, and generates pivalic acid as a readily separable byproduct. This mild, atom-economical strategy enables late-stage functionalization of pharmaceutical molecules, providing a sustainable route toward phenolic esters.

item.title: Base‐Catalyzed Cascade Reaction Between α‐Aminomaleimides and Electron‐Deficient Olefins: Syntheses of Aza‐Bicyclic Maleimides and Tricyclic Spiro‐Oxindoles
item.description:
A base-promoted cascade reaction of α-aminomaleimides via aza-Michael/S N 2′ and Michael-Nucleophilic addition pathways efficiently affords complex aza-bicyclic maleimides and tricyclic spiro-oxindoles frameworks in good yields and high diastereoselectivities.


A base-promoted aza-Michael/S N 2′ and Michael-Nucleophilic addition sequential reaction enables efficient preparations of aza-bicyclic maleimides and tricyclic spiro-oxindoles in generally good yields (up to 99% yield) with excellent diastereoselectivities (up to 20:1 dr) from α-aminomaleimides and electron-deficient olefins.

item.title: Synthesis of S‐Linked Glycoconjugates of Monosaccharides and Levoglucosenone Derivatives Through Photoinduced Thiol–Ene Reaction Mediated by 4CzIPN and Its Water Soluble Analog
item.description:
Visible-light thiol–ene reaction mediated by 4CzIPN enables access to hydrolytically stable S-linked glycoconjugates from levoglucosenone-derived thiols (Y = 91% to quant. d.r. = up to >95:5) and conventional thio-sugars (Y = 80% to quant. d.r. = up to >95:5).


Herein, we report a photoinduced thiol–ene reaction for the synthesis of S-linked glycoconjugates derived from levoglucosenone and related renewable glycosyl scaffolds (cyrene, levoglucosenone, and aminocyrene). They were converted into the corresponding thiol derivatives through novel synthetic routes inspired by standard sugar chemistry. Thus, the resulting thiols were efficiently engaged in photocatalyzed hydrothiolation reactions using the TADF (thermally activated delayed fluorescence) compound 4CzIPN under mild visible-light irradiation, affording a library of S-linked glycomimetic products in high to quantitative yields with the allyl alcohol, tetraethyl ethene-1,1-diylbis(phosphonate), and Fmoc-protected allyl glycine derivative as acceptors. The protocol was further translated to aqueous conditions by employing a water-soluble 4CzIPN analog, enabling the direct functionalization of deprotected thiol derivatives with acrylamide in water. Finally, the methodology was successfully extended to conventional gluco-, galacto-, and manno thiosugar analogs, demonstrating broad applicability, excellent functional group tolerance, and compatibility with both protected and unprotected carbohydrate substrates.

item.title: Sustainable Oxidation of Sulfides to Sulfoxides: Recent Advances in Catalyst Design and Oxygen‐Transfer Control (2021–2026)
item.description:
From earth-abundant metal-based systems to photoactive materials and electrochemical setups, this critical review explores how sulfide oxidation is being redesigned, showing how sustainability is gradually shifting from a desirable feature to a central consideration in modern organic chemistry.


Sustainable oxidation chemistry is not defined solely by the identity of the oxidant but by how oxygen transfer is controlled across the entire reaction system. In the case of sulfide oxidation, this challenge is particularly acute, as the selective formation of sulfoxides requires precise suppression of overoxidation pathways while maintaining functional-group tolerance and practical applicability. This review surveys advances from 2021 to 2026 in transformation of sulfides to sulfoxides, focusing on how modern catalytic platforms address this balance between selectivity and sustainability. Rather than adopting a purely methodological classification, the discussion is organized around catalyst design and activation modes, including earth-abundant metal catalysis, metal-free and metal-based photocatalysis, electrochemical systems, and organocatalytic oxygen-transfer processes. Across these approaches, key parameters—oxidant, solvent, catalyst loading and preparation, substrate scope, recyclability, scalability, and selectivity—are evaluated comparatively to identify the features that define genuinely sustainable protocols. Particular attention is paid to the increasing role of heterogeneous and structured materials, such as polymeric photocatalysts, covalent organic frameworks, and hybrid systems, which enable improved control over oxygen activation and catalyst recovery. By highlighting both recent advances and persistent limitations, this review provides a critical framework for understanding sulfide oxidation as model reaction for sustainable oxidation chemistry.

item.title: The Expanding Role of Diazirines in Synthetic Methodology
item.description:
Beyond their established role in photoaffinity labeling, diazirines have emerged as versatile reagents in synthetic chemistry. This review highlights their dual reactivity as carbene and nitrogen-transfer precursors, showcasing mechanistic insights and diverse applications in cyclopropanations, cycloadditions, skeletal editing, amination, heterocycle synthesis, and related transformations.


Diazirines are three-membered nitrogen-containing heterocycles best known as photochemical carbene precursors in photoaffinity labeling. Upon irradiation, diazirines undergo nitrogen extrusion to generate highly reactive carbenes capable of covalent bond insertion, a property that has been widely exploited in chemical biology and materials science. Despite their favorable handling properties compared to related diazo compounds and their versatility as both carbene precursors and nitrogen sources, diazirines have historically seen only limited application in synthetic organic chemistry. Over the past two decades, however, diazirines have increasingly emerged as valuable synthons in a broad range of transformations. Their applications can generally be divided into reactions exploiting either their carbene-generating properties or their ability to serve as nitrogen-transfer reagents. Diazirines have been employed in cyclopropanation and cyclopropenation reactions, cross-couplings, skeletal editing, glycosylations, reductive aminations, and the synthesis of nitrogen-containing heterocycles. Owing to their unique reactivity, diazirines can facilitate unusual or otherwise difficult-to-access transformations in organic synthesis. This review provides a comprehensive overview of diazirine-based synthetic methodologies, with particular emphasis on developments reported over the last two decades, and highlights future opportunities for their application in organic synthesis.

item.title: Azole‐Fused High‐Energy Heterocycles: A Decade of Synthetic Innovation and Structure–Property Insights (2015–2025)
item.description:
This review summarizes progress reported since 2015 on 97 azole-fused energetic heterocycles, including synthetic routes, density, detonation performance, thermal stability, and mechanical sensitivity. Representative advances in fused-ring construction and functionalization are summarized, while key strategic challenges in synthesizing complex fused nitrogen-rich frameworks and simultaneously achieving balanced overall performance are highlighted.


As modern weaponry and equipment evolve, there is an increasing demand for more powerful, less sensitive, and environmentally benign energetic materials. Fused heterocycle-based energetic materials, large conjugated systems composed of two or more rings that share adjacent atoms, exhibit superior thermal stability and higher density than their monocyclic and bridged analogs. Meanwhile, similar to cage heterocyclic rings, the fused structures generally possess higher heats of formation and elevated ring-strain energies, which enhance detonation performance. In addition, the fused backbones offer versatile modification sites, enabling researchers to balance energy and stability by introducing different functional groups. This review summarizes the research progress on 97 energetic fused heterocyclic compounds from the Web of Science (WOS) and Scopus databases since 2015 and presents their molecular design strategies, synthesis methods, and detonation properties. Furthermore, the major challenges are associated with the design of complex fused-ring frameworks and the large-scale preparation. This review highlights the insightful future research directions, particularly the development of universal synthesis strategies and the exploration of AI-driven automated design.

item.title: Recent Advances in Photochemical and Photoelectrochemical Fluoroalkylation: Direct Use of Fluoroalkyl Carboxylic Acids
item.description:
In this review, we highlight the latest advances in photochemical and photoelectrochemical fluoroalkylation methodologies that exploit fluoroalkyl carboxylic acids as straightforward, accessible, and practical fluoroalkylating reagents.


Extensive research has been dedicated to developing sustainable and practical methodologies for installing fluoroalkyl groups into organic molecules, as such structural modifications can effectively tune the physicochemical and pharmacological properties of drug candidates. Despite significant advances, most established fluoroalkylation protocols still suffer from inherent drawbacks: conventional fluoroalkylating reagents are often expensive, thermally or chemically labile, and difficult to handle. Furthermore, their practical implementation usually requires stoichiometric redox chemicals to facilitate the generation of operative fluoroalkylating intermediates, compromising functional group tolerance and atom economy and ultimately restricting applicability in large-scale synthesis. This review summarizes recent advances in fluoroalkylations using widely available fluoroalkyl carboxylic acids as direct fluoroalkyl radical precursors, highlighting the unique merits, synthetic scope, and future potential of this emerging strategy.

item.title: Main Group Acetylides in Copper(I)‐Catalyzed Azide–Alkyne Cycloaddition (CuAAC)
item.description:
All stable acetylides of the main group have been evaluated in copper-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC), and the competency with which they perform in CuAAC correlated with each main group element’s ability to perturb the electronics of its pendant alkyne, as evinced by infrared spectroscopy. Tin acetylides are identified as novel and competent substrates in CuAAC.


We report a systematic evaluation of 23 main group (MG) acetylides (Groups 13–17) in CuAAC, confirming prior MG acetylide reports and identifying tin acetylides as novel competent substrates in CuAAC. Optimized protocols for the corresponding triazolides were developed, and 1,4-regioselectivity was confirmed by single-crystal X-ray crystallography. Infrared spectroscopic analysis revealed that alkyne C≡C stretching frequencies decrease systematically upon descending any group, consistent with back-donation from the heteroatom into the alkyne π*-orbital and increased electron density at the β-carbon—features we propose are prerequisites for productive CuAAC. Acetylides of lighter elements (Si, Ge, B) undergo protonolysis under the reaction conditions rather than cycloaddition. Collectively, these results identify metal-like polarizability as the key criterion governing MG acetylide reactivity in CuAAC and provide a spectroscopic handle for predicting the behavior of heteroatom-substituted alkynes in this reaction.

item.title: Acid‐Promoted Divergent and Chemoselective Annulation of 2‐(Methylthio)‐2‐Thioxoacetates for the Synthesis of 4‐Oxo‐3,4‐Dihydroquinazolines and 4‐Oxo‐4H‐Benzo[d][1,3]thiazines
item.description:
A Brønsted acid-promoted divergent and chemoselective annulation of alkyl/arylmethyl 2 (methylthio)-2-thioxoacetate with 2-aminobenzamides provides efficient access to quinazolinones and benzothiazinones from common precursors. Product selectivity is controlled by the reaction medium under transition metal-free conditions, enabling broad substrate scope and excellent chemoselectivity.


A divergent and chemoselective method to quinazolinones and benzothiazinones has been developed through the reaction of alkyl/arylmethyl 2-(methylthio)-2-thioxoacetate with 2-aminobenzamides under Brønsted acid catalysis. The reaction delivered two structurally distinct heterocyclic scaffolds under different reaction conditions from a common synthetic precursor. The use of p-toluenesulfonic acid (p-TSA) in DMF afforded quinazolinone derivatives in good yields, while reactions performed in an AcOH/DMF (1:1) medium produced the corresponding benzothiazinones with excellent chemoselectivity. The methods demonstarte broad applicability under transition metal-free conditions. The structures and chemoselective cyclization of representative products were unequivocally furnished by spectroscopic characterization and single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis.

item.title: Indole‐ and Benzofuran‐Thioglycoside Synthesis via Palladium‐Catalyzed Migita/Larock Couplings: Synthesis and Photophysical Investigations
item.description:
A Pd-catalyzed Migita/Larock cross-coupling approach allows an efficient synthesis of indole- and benzofuran-thioglycosides as a new chemical space. Our synthetic strategy relies on the use of a 4-iodophenylethynyl motif as a bifunctional platform, enabling the sequential introduction of the glycosyl thiol moiety through a Pd-catalyzed C–S cross-coupling and the indole fragment via a Larock indole synthesis.


An efficient catalytic approach for the synthesis of novel indole- and benzofuran-thioglycoside derivatives by using simple cross-coupling reactions is established. The strategy involves two Pd-catalyzed cross-couplings including C─S bond-forming reaction between glycosyl thiols and p-iodoalkyne, followed by a Larock reaction. Following this catalytic approach, various indole- and benzofuran-containing thioglycoside derivatives were prepared with moderate to good yields (54%–84%). Among all thioglycoside derivatives synthesized, the fully acetylated N-Ts indole-derivative exhibits cytotoxicity against the human colon cancer cell line (HCT116) with an IC50 at the micromolecular level (6.94 ± 0.94 μM). Furthermore, the photophysical properties of all thioglycoside derivatives are studied.

item.title: Arylacetonitrile Meets Benzyl Bromide: Isothiouronium‐Mediated α‐Olefination Strategy for 2,3‐Diarylacrylonitriles
item.description:
Herein, we present an attractive strategy for the synthesis of (Z)-2,3-diarylacrylonitrile derivatives by acceptorless cross-dehydrogenative coupling between arylacetonitrile and benzyl bromide through isothiouronium salts. This α-olefination method is operationally simple and proceeds under open-air, metal-free conditions. With a broader substrate scope and high product yields, the developed protocol offers a useful strategy for synthesizing acrylonitrile derivatives for further academic and industrial exploration.


2,3-Diphenylacrylonitriles are widely used in synthetic and medicinal chemistry and have attracted considerable attention for their accessibility. Their synthetic approaches primarily employ metal-catalyzed coupling reactions between arylacetonitriles and alcohols. Herein, we present an attractive strategy for the synthesis of (Z)-2,3-diarylacrylonitrile derivatives by acceptorless cross-dehydrogenative coupling between arylacetonitrile and benzyl bromide through isothiouronium salts. This α-olefination method is operationally simple and proceeds under open-air, metal-free conditions. With a broader substrate scope and high product yields, the developed protocol offers a useful strategy for synthesizing acrylonitrile derivatives for further academic and industrial exploration.

item.title: Two‐Phase Electrochemical Vicinal Dibromination of Alkenes With Sodium Bromide as the Bromine Source and Supporting Electrolyte
item.description:
An efficient and concise method for two-phase electrochemical vicinal dibromination of alkenes using NaBr as a bromine source and electrolyte under mild, catalyst-free green conditions has been developed.


An environmentally friendly two-phase electrochemical method for the vicinal dibromination of alkenes has been developed. This strategy utilizes inexpensive sodium bromide as both the bromine source and the supporting electrolyte without the use of catalysts, external oxidants, and strong acids. It features simple operation, mild reaction conditions, broad substrate scope, and high efficiency, affording the desired products in up to 97% yield.

item.title: Synthesis of Flavones by Intramolecular O‐Arylation of Unactivated Halogenated Aryl‐1,3‐diketones
item.description:
A protocol for the synthesis of flavone derivatives starting from mono- and dihalogenated diketones including fluorinated derivatives in a very simple and effective way is reported.


Flavones are an important class of secondary metabolites in plants. Here we report a straightforward method for the conversion of unactivated halogenated 1,3-biaryl-1,3-diketones into chromenone derivatives via intramolecular O-arylation under mild conditions. The resulting flavones were obtained in excellent to moderate yields. The synthesis typically proceeds according to a SNAr mechanism under basic conditions without the requirement of any expensive catalyst. After successful implementation of fluorinated aryl diketones which lead to so far inaccessible fluoro-substituted flavones, the scope of the reaction was also extended to chlorinated and brominated substrates as well as to substances with electron-withdrawing or -donating substituents to demonstrate the functional group tolerance of the method. As an inverted reactivity was observed for bromo-chloro diketones, quantum chemical calculations have been applied to support the proposed concerted mechanism (cSNAr) for this case.

item.title: Visible‐Light‐Driven Regioselective Cross‐Dehydrogenative C–H Thio‐ and Selenocyanation of Indolo[1,2‐a]quinoxalines Under Photocatalyst‐, Oxidant‐ and Metal‐Free Aerobic Conditions
item.description:
An atom-economical, functional-group-tolerant method is reported for the visible-light-mediated thio- and selenocyanation of a variety of indoloquinoxalines under aerobic conditions at ambient temperature.


A visible-light-promoted cross-dehydrogenative protocol has been developed for the regioselective thiocyanation and selenocyanation of indolo[1,2-a]quinoxaline derivatives. This photoinduced transformation proceeds at ambient temperature under metal-free aerobic conditions without using an external oxidant and any photosensitizer. The key features of this protocol, including high yields, excellent regioselectivity, operational simplicity, broad functional group tolerance, and scalability, make it a synthetically attractive and practical method.

item.title: Recent Advances in Functional Group Transpositions in Arenes and Heteroarenes
item.description:
Recent advances in functional group transposition in arenes and heteroarenes are reviewed. Representative strategies, including transition-metal-enabled dissociation–recombination sequences, carbocation-mediated processes, photochemical heterocycle isomerizations, and multistep relay approaches, are discussed. Current limitations and future opportunities for the development and application of these transformations are also highlighted.


Functional group transpositions in arenes and heteroarenes constitute a powerful tool in organic synthesis, enabling access to synthetically elusive compounds. Classical aromatic rearrangements, such as the Smiles, Claisen, and Bamberger reactions, allow positional reorganization but inevitably leave a residual substituent at the original ipso carbon, thereby precluding complete transfer. In contrast, a conceptually distinct yet underdeveloped class of transformations enables genuine positional transposition, in which a substituent undergoes net positional relocation within a pre-existing or newly formed aromatic framework, thereby generating a different substitution pattern in the final aromatic product. This review delineates the conceptual boundaries among these processes and organizes previously scattered examples of functional group transposition, including transition-metal-enabled dissociation–recombination sequences, carbocation-mediated processes, and multistep relay strategies, while also discussing closely related photochemical heterocycle isomerizations involving aromatic ring reconstruction as complementary strategies for positional editing. These advances highlight new opportunities to overcome intrinsic site-selectivity limitations in aromatic synthesis.

item.title: Unorthodox Applications of Diethylaminosulfur Trifluoride and its Analogs in Organic Synthesis
item.description:
Unorthodox applications of DAST-type reagents extend beyond classical deoxyfluorination, encompassing the synthesis of diverse fluoroalkylated scaffolds as well as nonfluorinated products, thereby expanding their synthetic utility and offering new opportunities for organic synthesis, medicinal chemistry, and drug discovery.


Diethylaminosulfur trifluoride (DAST) and related reagents are well-established, commercially available nucleophilic fluorinating agents primarily known for their effectiveness in deoxyfluorination. Beyond their conventional applications, DAST-type reagents have recently emerged as versatile tools for the synthesis of CF3S-containing compounds, fluorinated benzoxathiin derivatives, and other non-fluorine-containing molecules that hold significant interest in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and materials science. This review highlights the reactivity and expanding synthetic utility of DAST-type reagents, with a particular emphasis on their unique roles in novel chemical transformations.

item.title: Direct Synthesis of α‐Amino Ketones From Aldehydes and Amines via Photocatalytic In Situ Imines Hydroacylation
item.description:
A hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) photocatalytic approach has been developed for the direct synthesis of α-amino ketones from aldehydes and amines, featuring high atom- and step-economy, simple operation, good sustainability, and better practicality.


α-Amino ketones have essential applications in pharmaceuticals and organic synthesis. The hydroacylation of imines is an attractive approach to access such valuable compounds. However, existing methods for hydroacylation with readily available aldehydes are highly dependent on the prepreparation of imines. Here, we report a photocatalytic protocol for synthesizing α-amino ketones directly from aldehydes and amines. This one-pot reaction proceeds smoothly in the presence of the photocatalyst tetrabutylammonium decatungstate (TBADT) and catalytic amounts of HBr. Aldehydes serve as both precursors for in situ imine formation and subsequent acylating agents. Hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) photocatalysis exhibits excellent two-stage compatibility, allowing the transformation under mild and simple conditions. This strategy avoids the prepreparation and isolation of imines, providing an atom- and step-economical route for the convenient synthesis of α-amino ketones.

item.title: Enantioselective Conjugate Addition of Malononitriles to Enynes: A Stereodivergent Approach to Chiral Allenes
item.description:
Quinine-catalyzed enantioselective conjugate addition of malononitrile derivatives to enynes provides trisubstituted chiral allenes in good to excellent yields and high enantiopurities under mild conditions. Broad substrate scope, easy scalability, and versatile post-synthetic transformations into enantioenriched pyrazoles and furans highlight the synthetic utility of this methodology.


Quinine-catalyzed enantioselective conjugate addition of malononitrile derivatives to enynes enables stereodivergent synthesis of trisubstituted chiral allenes. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions with good to excellent yields and high enantiomeric purities for both diastereoisomers. Optimization revealed that solvent and temperature strongly influence reactivity and stereochemical outcome. A broad range of aromatic and aliphatic enynes, as well as α-substituted malononitriles, are well tolerated. The method is amenable to scale-up and allows efficient derivatization of the resulting allenes into enantioenriched pyrazoles and furans, providing versatile building blocks for asymmetric synthesis.

item.title: Ammonium Chloride and Peroxide: A Metal‐Free Aqueous Strategy for Oxime Synthesis
item.description:
A metal-free aqueous strategy using NH4Cl/H2O2 with monoethanolamine enables oxime synthesis from carbonyls, tolerating 55 substrates (up to 93% yield) and gram-scale production, providing a green, cost-effective approach.


A metal-free, aqueous protocol enables the synthesis of oximes from carbonyls using NH4Cl and H2O2. A radical mechanism involving in situ hydroxylamine generation bypasses the use of unstable salts. Monoethanolamine (MEA) serves as an essential additive, facilitating the conversion of 55 substrates with yields up to 93%. The practicality is underscored by a room-temperature gram-scale synthesis that requires no chromatographic purification, establishing a cost-effective and environmentally benign alternative for oxime production.

item.title: Navigating the Radical Oxo‐Functionalization of Alkenes Toward Ketones
item.description:
Straightforward access to complex ketones in a single synthetic step: This Review surveys the latest advances in three-component alkene 1,2-oxo-functionalizations. The opportunities unlocked by the so-called single-electron (1e–) logic, including access to a broad pool of radical precursors and carbonyl oxygen atom sources, are highlighted. Transition metal-catalyzed, photochemical, and electrochemical cascade processes that enable the sequential installation of CX and CO bonds across a CC double bond are critically discussed.


Ketones are ubiquitous structural motifs in pharmaceuticals, natural products, agrochemicals, and functional materials, as well as indispensable building blocks in organic synthesis. This outlines the design of efficient carbonyl-forming strategies a crucial target in methodology development. Alongside classical textbook polar, two electron (2e–) approaches, the so-called single-electron (1e–) logic has established itself as the contemporary method of choice for direct, de novo construction of structurally complex ketones from simple commodity chemicals, under mild conditions. In this context, radical 1,2-oxo-functionalization of alkenes represents a valuable, practical platform to rapidly enhance molecular complexity via one-pot difunctionalization of “flat” feedstock chemicals, thereby avoiding tedious isolation and purification of intermediates en route to target ketones. This Review surveys recent advances in radical alkene oxo-functionalization, with a particular emphasis on methodologies enabled by thermal, transition metal-catalyzed, photochemical, and electrochemical activations. The mechanistic principles governing the finely-tuned orchestration of sequential vicinal CX (with X = carbon or heteroatom) and CO bond formations—including single-electron transfer, hydrogen atom transfer, and radical polar crossover—are discussed alongside the diverse carbonyl oxygen atom sources employed, such as tert-butyl hydroperoxide (TBHP), dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), and molecular oxygen (O2).

item.title: Copper(II)/4‐Dimethylaminopyridine‐Mediated Oxidative Cyclization in Low‐Melting Mixtures: Access to Cyclopropane‐Fused Aza‐Heterocycles
item.description:
Therapeutically important 3-azabicyclo[n.1.0]alkanes were prepared from readily accessible N-allyl/homoallyl-malonamates by oxidative cyclization, involving single-electron transfer, in a deep eutectic solvent. The protocol was extended to active methylene amides, including phenylsulfonylacetamide, to access cyclopropane-fused aza-heterocycles, and the strategy enabled the concise synthesis of the antidepressant drug candidate GSK1360707.


A simple and efficient one-pot approach has been developed for the stereoselective synthesis of 3-azabicyclo[n.1.0]alkane derivatives, employing a low–melting mixture (LMM) composed of choline chloride (ChCl) and N,N-dimethylurea (DMU). This green and sustainable protocol facilitates the intramolecular oxidative cyclization of N-allyl malonamates to afford a diverse array of cyclopropane-fused aza-heterocycles in excellent yields. Furthermore, the utility of this methodology is exemplified in the concise and efficient synthesis of the antidepressant drug candidate GSK1360707.

item.title: Spring‐Loaded p‐Block Ions: Homodesmotic Ring Strain Energy Benchmarks for Charged Three‐Membered Rings
item.description:
Accurate RSE (ring strain energies) are reported for saturated ionic three-membered rings involving one charged heteroelement of groups 13, 15, 16, or 17, after a thorough study for evaluating the most reliable set of homodesmotic reactions. RSE trends along the groups, periods, and hybridization state of the heteroelement are analyzed. RSE are also dissected into additive strain contributions of atoms and bonds.


Ring strain energy (RSE) is central to the stability and ring-opening chemistry of three-membered rings (3MRs), yet reliable benchmarks for ionic p-block 3MRs remain scarce. Here, we establish a unified homodesmotic protocol for charged saturated 3MRs: monocationic pnictogeniranium, chalcogeniranium and halonium ions, and monoanionic trieliranides bearing H, F, or Me ligands. A three-tier workflow, from GFN2-xTB screening to DLPNO-CCSD(T)/def2-QZVPP refinement, is used to compare counter-ion-free reactions, Coulomb-corrected charge-separated products and explicit ion pairs with SbF6 − or Cs+. Benchmarking shows that naked-ion C─C cleavage, or the average of naked-ion C─C and C─El cleavages where appropriate, gives the most transferable RSE scale while avoiding artifacts from ion pairing. Cationic 3MRs are generally more strained than their neutral analogs, whereas trieliranides show stronger substituent control, with fluorination markedly increasing RSE. The heaviest pnictogeniranium cations (As, Sb, Bi) are best described as pseudocyclic, nonclassical multicentre C2Pn frameworks lacking an RCP and displaying Dewar–Chatt–Duncanson-type structures. Periodic trends are rationalized through lone-pair-driven hybridization changes and charge-dependent bonding. Additive atom and bond strain contributions are reported to enable rapid estimation of RSE in charged p-block 3MRs.

item.title: Rigidification of 7‐Aminocoumarins Bearing Electron‐Withdrawing Groups Increases Emission Intensity in Polar Environments
item.description:
The heretofore unknown amino-coumarin-lactams maintain strong emission in polar aprotic solvents. The combined experimental and computational study revealed that blocking free rotation of electron-withdrawing substituent at position 4 plays a key role in the fate of these molecules in the excited state.


A set of structurally unique coumarins possessing an amino group at position 7 and lactam ring fused to the coumarin lactone ring were synthesized for the first time via Pechmann reaction. The photophysics of these new polarized donor–acceptor dyes were compared with those of structural analogs bearing an ester and amide groups at position 4, revealing significant differences in absorption/emission maxima, solvatofluorochromism and emission intensity. Emission of coumarin-lactams is blue in cyclohexane and orange in MeOH, whereas coumarin-esters emit cyan light in cyclohexane and red light in MeOH. Crucially, rigidification of coumarin-lactams’ skeleton combined with replacement of ester with amide functionality has a profound effect on emission intensity decrease in polar solvents: even in acetonitrile, fluorescence quantum yields are still around 50%. Computational studies probed the nature of the key excited states of all dyes and enabled us to venture the hypothesis that blocking free rotation of electron-withdrawing group at position 4 is responsible for controlling non-radiative dissipation of energy in more polar solvents.

item.title: Gold‐Catalyzed Cyclization of Indole‐Tethered Alkynes Enabling Synthesis of Exocyclic Alkenyl Tetrahydrocarbazoles
item.description:
An efficient gold-catalyzed intramolecular cyclization of indole-tethered alkynes using AgNTf2 as an additive has been developed, which provides bioactive exocyclic alkenyl tetrahydrocarbazoles with up to 85% yield. Control experiments and DFT studies indicate that the reaction proceeds via a 6-exo-dig cyclization pathway, with gold acetylide complexes as key intermediates and HE as a base.


A gold-catalyzed intramolecular cyclization of indole-tethered alkynes using Hantzsch ester (HE) and AgNTf2 as additives has been developed, providing diverse functionalized exocyclic alkenyl tetrahydrocarbazoles in good to excellent yields. Control experiments and DFT studies indicate that the reaction proceeds via a 6-exo-dig cyclization pathway, with gold acetylide complexes as key intermediates and HE serving as a base. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions, shows broad functional-group tolerance, and is amenable to scale-up. Selected tetrahydrocarbazole products also exhibited moderate antifungal activity against two forest pathogenic fungi.

item.title: Electrochemical Synthesis of Sulfur(VI) Compounds
item.description:
Sulfur(VI) motifs are widely found in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and materials science. Electrochemical synthesis offers a sustainable route to these valuable scaffolds by replacing conventional oxidants with electric current. This review highlights recent advances in the electrochemical synthesis of diverse S(VI) compounds under mild and practical conditions.


Electrochemical synthesis is emerging as a green and versatile platform for sulfur(VI) chemistry, using electric current to replace or minimize the use of stoichiometric oxidants and to access high-valent sulfur under generally mild conditions. This review highlights recent (2020–2025) electrochemical methods for the preparation of key S(VI) motifs, including sulfonyl fluorides, sulfones, sulfonate esters, thiosulfonates, sulfoximines, and sulfonimidoyl fluorides. Emphasis is placed on the transformation of simple S-containing precursors in straightforward undivided or flow cell setups under mild conditions, highlighting electrosynthesis as a sustainable tool for constructing and editing sulfur(VI) scaffolds relevant to medicinal chemistry, agrochemicals, and materials science.

item.title: Click Bioconjugation of Aza‐BODIPY Fluorophores to LfcinB Peptides for Improved Biocompatibility
item.description:
Click bioconjugation attaches NIR aza-BODIPY fluorophores to LfcinB-derived anticancer peptides via CuAAC and thiol-maleimide chemistry. Conjugates exhibit improved predicted solubility while retaining strong NIR absorption (703–730 nm). Peptide-aza-BODIPY conjugates induce apoptotic morphology in HeLa cancer cells.


Near-infrared (NIR) organic fluorophores have emerged as promising for biomedical imaging and theragnostics, offering deep-tissue penetration and reduced background interference. However, poor aqueous solubility and limitations in photostability, biocompatibility, and targeting hinder in vivo applications. Similarly, antimicrobial and anticancer peptides exhibit proteolytic instability and rapid clearance. This study addresses these issues by covalently bioconjugating aza-BODIPY fluorophores with LfcinB-derived peptides (RRWQWR, RWQWRWQWR) using CuAAC and thiol-maleimide click chemistries. Two strategies were compared: (i) CuAAC between azide/alkyne-functionalized partners, and (ii) Michael addition with cysteine-containing peptides and AZB-maleimide. Bioconjugation significantly improved water solubility (calculated LogP 5.3–5.5 → 1.1–4.2; LogS −8.2 → −2.2/−3.7) while preserving NIR photophysical properties (λ ab s = 703–730 nm). In silico ADMET analysis provided preliminary support for favorable predicted absorption-related properties and metabolic stability. Thiol-maleimide constructs showed superior predicted solubility, lower mutagenicity, and more favorable synthetic accessibility than CuAAC analogs. Phase-contrast microscopy of HeLa cells revealed characteristic apoptotic morphology (cell rounding/shrinkage, membrane association) with blue staining reflecting aza-BODIPY localization. In parallel, P12 induced caspase activation in flow cytometry assays, providing preliminary evidence of caspase-associated apoptotic activity. Collectively, these platforms provide a basis for the further development of NIR probes, although their in vivo performance remains to be established experimentally.

item.title: Copper‐Catalyzed One‐Pot Approach to 6‐Membered Sultams From Vinyl Sulfonamide Using Methanol as C1 Building Block
item.description:
A CuBr2-catalyzed oxidative coupling of vinyl sulfonamides with methanol efficiently constructs taurultams under ambient, air-tolerant conditions. Serving dually as solvent and sustainable C1 source, methanol enables diverse 6-membered sultams to be delivered in high yields with broad functional group tolerance, offering an operationally simple, scalable, and practical approach to taurultam synthesis.


A CuBr2-catalyzed one-pot oxidative coupling of vinyl sulfonamides with methanol has been developed for the efficient construction of taurultams. Methanol functions dually as solvent and C1 source, while H2O2 serves as a benign oxidant. The reaction proceeds under ambient conditions without inert atmosphere requirements, demonstrating excellent functional group tolerance and delivering diverse sultams in high yields. This operationally straightforward protocol demonstrates that copper-catalyzed activation of methanol enables its utilization as a sustainable C1 building block for taurultam synthesis, establishing a scalable and practical route to 6-membered sultam scaffolds.

item.title: Hydrosilylation of Nitrones With Trichlorosilane: Preparation of Hydroxylamines
item.description:
An inherent directing group enabled hydrosilylation of nitrones with trichlorosilane has been unprecedentedly developed, providing an efficient and transition metal-free method for the synthesis of hydroxylamines.


Herein, we describe a novel catalyst- and transition-metal-free method for the hydrosilylation of nitrones with trichlorosilane. A variety of hydroxylamines (38 examples) were obtained in moderate to good yields (28%–88%) with broad substrate compatibility under mild and operationally simple conditions. Control experiments confirm that the inherent directing groups of nitrones plays a pivotal role in bridging the reactants and facilitating the reaction. Furthermore, the synthetic utility of this method is demonstrated by gram-scale synthesis and elaboration of the products.

item.title: Microwave‐Assisted Copper‐Mediated One‐Pot Sequential Synthesis of Quinolino[3,4‐b]quinoxalines
item.description:
A microwave-assisted CuI-mediated one-pot tandem annulation enables rapid and scalable synthesis of quinolino[3,4-b]quinoxalines from 2-(2-bromophenyl)quinoxalines with aldehydes or benzyl alcohols using TMSN3, affording diverse products in up to 91% yield.


An efficient microwave-assisted one-pot protocol has been developed for the synthesis of 6-aryl/heteroarylquinolino[3,4-‍b]quinoxaline derivatives. The method involves a CuI-mediated tandem annulation of 2-(2-bromophenyl)quinoxalines with aryl and heteroaryl aldehydes, using TMSN3 as the nitrogen source. The transformation proceeds rapidly under microwave irradiation, delivering the desired products in moderate-to-excellent yields (up to 91%) with broad substrate scope. Further, benzyl alcohols (with TBHP) also serve as viable precursors under identical conditions to afford 6-aryl/heteroaryl-quinolino[3,4-b]quinoxaline derivatives. Notably, the protocol eliminates the requirement for a stoichiometric amount of reducing agent used in the earlier protocol. It can be extended to gram-scale synthesis with a remarkably reduced reaction time. Mechanistic investigations, supported by control experiments, ESI-HRMS analysis, and DFT calculations, provide insight into the reaction pathway. This approach offers a rapid, practical, and scalable route to quinolino[3,4-b]quinoxaline frameworks of potential medicinal relevance.

item.title: Temperature‐Dependent Regiodivergent [3 + 2] Cycloaddition of Azomethine Ylides With (E)‐5‐Benzylidenethioxoimidazolidin‐4‐One
item.description:
An efficient route is developed to get access to novel dispiro[imidazolidine-4,1′-pyrrolo[2,1-a] isoquinoline-3′,3″-indoline]-2″,5-dione skeletons by a one-pot three-component [3 + 2] cycloaddition reaction of (E)-5-benzylidenethioxoimidazolidin-4-ones, isatin derivatives, and 1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinoline (THIQ).


An efficient route is developed to gain access to novel dispiro[imidazolidine-4,1′-pyrrolo[2,1-a] isoquinoline-3′,3″-indoline]-2″,5-dione skeletons by a one-pot three-component [3 + 2] cycloaddition reaction of (E)-5-benzylidenethioxoimidazolidin-4-ones, isatin derivatives, and 1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinoline. Interestingly we note that the reaction‘s regioselectivity depends on temperature, enabling the production of two regioisomericdispiro[imidazolidine-4,1′-pyrrolo[2,1-a] isoquinoline-3′,3″-indoline]-2″,5-dione in high yield. In agreement with the experimental results, density functional theory calculations carried out at the 6-31+g*(d,p)5 level of theory predicted that the [3 + 2] cycloaddition processes occur in an asynchronous concerted manner.

item.title: Sunscreens as Organic Energy Materials: Macroscopic Heat Release Through Vibrational Relaxation Mechanism
item.description:
We show for the first time that ACHI derivatives can effectively convert UV and sunlight into heat in solid coatings, raising temperatures by up to 15 °C. These transparent materials are durable under prolonged UV exposure and work best when applied as uniform thin films. Their efficient light-to-heat conversion makes them promising candidates for smart windows and other energy-management technologies.


Aminocyclohexenimine (ACHI) derivatives are powerful UV-absorbing molecules, long recognized for their unique properties as sunscreens. Here, we demonstrate for the first time the macroscopic heat release through the previously proposed vibrational relaxation mechanism at the molecular level. Thin films of four different ACHI derivatives deposited on quartz substrates produced measurable macroscopic temperature increases (up to 15 °C) under UV and simulated solar irradiation and moderate-to-excellent photothermal stability (maximum half-life of 116 h under continuous UV). While drop-cast films provided proof of concept, spin coating yielded transparent and homogeneous layers that enabled direct monitoring of both thermal and spectroscopic responses in the solid state. These experiments revealed that solid-state absorption spectra, rather than solution-phase properties, correlate best with photothermal performance. The combination of transparency, durability, and efficient light-to-heat conversion highlights ACHI derivatives as a pioneering family of organic photothermal coatings, with potential applications in energy-managing and optically transparent technologies such as smart windows.

item.title: Competing Charge Transport Pathways: A Spirobifluorene‐Based Molecular Loop
item.description:
A rigid molecular loop integrating a spirobifluorene (SBF) core with a cycloparaphenylene (CPP) moiety provides two distinct transport channels. Through-space spiroconjugation and radial π-conjugation along a CPP backbone coexist within a single molecule. Preliminary single-molecule charge transport studies reveal multiple conductance features.


Understanding the relationship between molecular structure and charge transport remains a crucial aspect towards integrating single molecules into electronic devices, especially in systems which feature multiple conducting pathways. Here we report the synthesis of a molecular loop that incorporates a rigid 9,9′-spirobifluorene (SBF) core as a central mounting point for thiol anchoring groups and a cycloparaphenylene (CPP) backbone. The model compound is synthesized by a Suzuki–Miyaura coupling between a CPP precursor and a functionalized SBF derivative, followed by reductive aromatization of the macrocycle. The resulting macrocycles are fully characterized and enantiomerically resolved by chiral high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), and their chiroptical properties are investigated. Conductance measurements in a mechanically controlled break-junction (MCBJ) setup demonstrate reproducible single-molecule junction formation with two dominant conductance plateaus near 2 × 10−4 G0 and 4 × 10−5 G0, observed across different samples and applied voltages. The observed conductance features are consistent with multiple reproducible junction configurations, highlighting the molecular loop as a promising platform for studying charge transport through multiple intramolecular pathways.

item.title: Direct Conversion of Aryl Iodides Into Benzylamines by Aminomethylation: Reaction Scope, Mechanistic Studies, and Applications
item.description:
This study presents an efficient aminomethylation of aryl iodides with formamides for the synthesis of benzylamines using a reusable palladium catalyst at a loading of 65 mol ppm. The substrate scope is systematically evaluated, and mechanistic investigations provide insight into the reaction pathway and the origin of the observed catalytic efficiency.


Despite the high utility and value of benzylamines and their derivatives, their synthesis is hindered by a limited substrate availability and nonreusable transition-metal catalysts. To that end, this study develops an aminomethylation strategy using aryl iodides and formamides while examining the substrate scope and underlying mechanism for synthesizing benzylamines under parts-per-million-level (65 ppm) reusable palladium catalysis. This method can accommodate a wide range of substrates, including electron-rich and electron-deficient aryl, polyaryl, and heteroaryl iodides. Similarly, various formamide derivatives yield aminomethylated products. This aminomethylation strategy is used to directly synthesize biologically active molecules, such as a rivastigmine analog, and natural products, e.g., gramine. In addition, tryptamine, a serotonin receptor, and diindolylmethane, a metabolite, are successfully produced by derivatizing the aminomethylated products. Isotope-labeling experiments indicate that formamide derivatives were precursors for the reducing agent, in addition to providing both amines and carbon. A plausible catalytic pathway is proposed based on isotope-labeling experiments and density functional theory calculations, providing insights for future research and new applications in organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry.

item.title: Solid‐State Melt Rearrangement/Acetylation Reaction of Primary Amides and PhI(OAc)2 in Reactive Eutectic Medium
item.description:
A substrates-involved reactive eutectic rearrangement/acetylation reaction from primary amides and PhI(OAc)2 without any solvents was developed. This reaction features lower temperature, shorter time, higher efficiency, and simpler operation.


A novel solid-state melt rearrangement reaction from primary amides and PhI(OAc)2 without any solvents in reactive eutectic medium was established. Compared with traditional solvent-involved or high-temperature solid-state reactions, this reaction features lower temperature, shorter time, and higher efficiency. Especially for the aliphatic diamides and PhI(OAc)2, they could easily form a reactive eutectic mixture and undergo double Hofmann-type rearrangement reactions, giving the diamine diacetylated products in high yields. Notably, the products can be easily isolated through a direct precipitation–filtration method.

item.title: A Novel Scaffold for Liquid Phase Peptide Synthesis
item.description:
A novel, Lys-PEG-based support allows (i) the avoidance of polystyrene resins, (ii) the use of more eco-friendly solvents, not accessible to SPPS, (iii) the running of the syntheses in a homogeneous phase. Purification after each coupling and cleavage of the protecting groups are performed by organic nanofiltration.


The growing number of peptides approved as drugs is pushing the introduction of synthetic methodologies alternative to the solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS), currently the most exploited method for large-scale peptide production. Indeed, SPPS is easily scalable, can be automated, and allows the synthesis of long peptides in short times. However, it also has some disadvantages, as it uses large excesses of reagents, huge amounts of solvents (often not “green”), a non-biodegradable solid support, and features a heterogeneous reaction environment in which amino acid couplings are more difficult than in a homogeneous environment. For this reason, in recent years there has been growing interest in developing better synthetic methods. In this work, we present a new dendrimeric support based on lysine (Lys) and short polyethylene glycol (PEG) chains. Its main advantages are (i) the possibility of using more eco-friendly solvents that cannot be used in standard SPPS, (ii) the replacement of polystyrene-based supports with a PEG-lysine hybrid one, and (iii) the formation of a homogeneous reaction medium that will help to reduce the excess of reagents and solvents. The results obtained in the synthesis of a model peptide are promising and amenable to transfer to an industrial scale.

item.title: Visible‐Light‐Mediated Synthesis of Biscoumarins Utilizing Photocaged Sulfonic Acid as the Catalyst
item.description:
A mild visible light approach for the synthesis of biscoumarins utilizing arylazo sulfones as the photoacid generator under 467 nm irradiation is introduced.


Throughout the years, biscoumarin derivatives, known for their diverse biological properties, have attracted extensive synthetic interest. In pursuit of a sustainable, versatile, and cost-effective protocol, we studied the reaction between 4-hydroxycoumarin and various aldehydes, using arylazo sulfones as the photoacid generators. Hence, we developed a mild, visible-light-driven approach for the synthesis of biscoumarins, utilizing arylazo sulfones under 467 nm irradiation, affording products in moderate-to-high yields. The effectiveness and the limited waste production of our protocol, combined with its simplicity, including the purification by recrystallization, highlight its great potential for pharmaceutical applications.

item.title: c‐Met/DDR1 Dual‐Target Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor Featuring an Imidazo[1,2‐A]pyridine Core
item.description:
In this contribution, we report a novel tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) based on bioisosteric replacement of cabozantinib’s pharmacophore fragment with an imidazo[1,2-a]pyridine scaffold. The best compound, 10a, exhibited up to 2.6 μM IC50 against the cancer cell line HepG2. The inhibition selectivity profile assay demonstrated that 10a is a c-Met/DDR1 dual-target TKI.


In this contribution, we report the design, synthesis, and bioactivity evaluation of a novel class of dual-target tyrosine kinases inhibitors (TKIs). By linking imidazo[1,2-a]pyridines with a commonly used cyclopropanecarboxylic acid pharmacophore fragment, a number of novel potential TKIs were synthesized. Aryl and heteroaryl side chains with different electron-withdrawing groups and electron-donating groups were introduced to the imidazo[1,2-a]pyridine ring to evaluate the inhibitory effects against Huh-7 and HepG2 tumor cells. The research results showed that compound 10a with a pyridine side-chain exhibited better in vitro inhibitory effects against Huh-7 and HepG2 cells than cabozantinib. Cell cloning and cell scratch experiments indicated that 10a significantly hampered the tumor cell proliferation and migration and exhibited comparable cytotoxicity against normal cells. Through a selectivity profile study on a 217 kinase panel, cellular-mesenchymal epithelial transition factor (c-Met) and discoidin domain receptor 1 (DDR1) were identified to be the potential targets of compound 10a.

item.title: Synthesis and Antiviral Evaluation of Sugar‐Modified Pseudouridine Analogs
item.description:
Sugar-modified nucleoside analogs of pseudouridine, which is a natural C-nucleoside, were synthesized. Antiviral screening identified weak to moderate inhibitors of Zika and dengue viruses (compounds 10, 11, 14, and 15). ProTide prodrugs of the lead compounds failed to enhance potency, suggesting that future work should focus on triphosphate analogs to investigate viral polymerase inhibition.


The pyrimidine C-nucleoside pseudouridine (Ψ) is a ubiquitous RNA modification that enhances the stability, modulates immunogenicity, and influences the biological function of natural and synthetic RNA. Despite its biological importance, the antiviral potential of pseudouridine analogs remains largely unexplored. Furthermore, although several sugar-modified pseudouridine analogs have been synthesized, a systematic approach to access these derivatives is still lacking. In this study, we present the synthesis of novel pseudouridine analogs with structural modifications at different positions of the carbohydrate moiety.

item.title: Synthesis, Structure, and Physicochemical Properties of Doubly Fused Phenoxazine‐Embedded Dithiasapphyrins
item.description:
Novel doubly fused phenoxazine-embedded dithiasapphyrins were synthesized via an acid-catalyzed (3 + 2) condensation reaction. X-ray crystallographic analysis revealed an unusual bithiophene ring inversion and the formation of two fused tripentacyclic rings within the macrocyclic framework.


Herein, we report the synthesis of a new class of doubly fused phenoxazine-embedded dithiasapphyrins via (3 + 2) condensation of an appropriate phenoxazine-based tripyrrane with bithiophene diol in CH2Cl2 under BF3·OEt2-catalyzed conditions. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis of one representative macrocycle revealed an unusual structural rearrangement involving inversion of the two thiophene rings of the bithiophene unit, followed by fusion of the inner thiophene carbon atoms with adjacent pyrrolic nitrogen atoms to generate two tripentacyclic fused rings within the dithiasapphyrin framework. The resulting macrocycle adopts a highly distorted conformation, with the phenoxazine unit deviating by 66.97° from the mean plane defined by the four meso-carbon atoms. These doubly fused phenoxazine-embedded dithiasapphyrins exhibit intense panchromatic absorption across the UV–visible region with pronounced bathochromic shifts relative to their previously reported phenothiazine-fused analogues. Protonation with TFA further extends the absorption profile into the UV–visible-near-infrared region, affording strongly red-shifted diprotonated species. Electrochemical studies revealed that the phenoxazine-fused macrocycles are more electron-rich than the corresponding phenothiazine derivatives. Density functional theory and time-dependent density functional theory studies support the experimental observations.

item.title: Recent Advances in CH Bond Functionalization Using Traceless N‐Functionalized Directing Groups
item.description:
H Bond Functionalization Using Traceless N-Functionalized Directing Groups"/>

This review focuses on the development of diverse traceless N-functionalized directing groups and their application in the CH bond functionalization. Typical examples that use N-functionalized TDGs, such as N-oxides, nitrones, N-nitroso groups, hydrazyl groups, N-acyl groups, and other nitrogen-functionalized groups, have been documented in this review.


The chelation-assisted CH bond activation with proper directing groups not only promotes the reaction efficiency but also enables selective CC or CX bond formation at the specific positions. Among them, the traceless directing groups (TDGs) strategy is highly attractive since it allows the in situ removal of directing groups after the directed CH bond functionalization. On the other hand, N-containing substrates, e.g., N-heterocycles, amines, and oximes, are of great importance in both organic synthesis and drug discovery. The directed site-selective CH bond functionalization of nitrogen-based substrates using TDG strategy constitutes an ideal solution to access more elaborate molecules. In this context, this review focus on the development of diverse traceless N-functionalized directing groups and their application in the CH bond functionalization, along with mechanistic insights into the directing group removal steps. Typical examples that use N-functionalized TDGs, such as N-oxides, nitrones, N-nitroso groups, hydrazyl groups, N-acyl groups, and other nitrogen-functionalized groups, have been documented in this review, aiming to give a timely comprehensive overview and stimulate the development of more efficient methodologies.

item.title: Synthetic Applications of Hypervalent Iodine Reagents in Multicomponent Reactions
item.description:
Hypervalent iodine reagents participate in and mediate diverse multicomponent reactions. This review highlights recent advances involving acyclic iodine(III) reagents, cyclic hypervalent iodine reagents, diaryliodonium salts, and iodine(V) reagents, with emphasis on their distinct activation modes and synthetic applications.


Multicomponent reactions (MCRs) provide an efficient strategy for the rapid assembly of structurally diverse molecules from simple starting materials in a one-pot manner. Meanwhile, hypervalent iodine reagents have emerged as versatile and environmentally benign reagents owing to their unique oxidative properties and diverse activation modes. The merger of hypervalent iodine chemistry with MCRs has enabled numerous efficient transformations involving oxidative activation, radical relay processes, electrophilic group transfer, and carbynoid chemistry. This review summarizes recent advances in hypervalent iodine-mediated MCRs involving acyclic iodine(III) reagents, cyclic hypervalent iodine reagents, diaryliodonium salts, and iodine(V) reagents.

item.title: Exploiting Biocatalysis for the Scalable Synthesis of Enantiopure γ‐Hydroxynitrile Building Blocks
item.description:
Screening a panel of (S)-and (R)-selective alcohol dehydrogenases identified several biocatalysts for stereoselectively reducing γ-ketonitriles into γ-hydroxynitriles. These processes were optimized, delivering the targets in yields up to 88% with e.e.’s up to 99%. Scalability of the methodology was achieved to produce gram quantities of product, which enabled the unambiguous assignment of absolute stereochemistry by single X-ray diffraction.


We report the scalable biocatalyzed synthesis of γ-hydroxynitriles from their corresponding prochiral ketone precursors. Screening of a panel of alcohol dehydrogenases (ADHs) identified RRADH as an (S)-selective ADH yielding the desired products in e.e. values of 99%, whereas LSADH gave (R)-configured γ-hydroxynitriles (e.e. up to 95%). Optimization of this transformation allowed for reaction scale-up to 5 mmol, affording the targets in gram quantities. Moreover, the absolute configuration of the (S)-configured products was unambiguously established by single-crystal diffraction. This study showcases how chiral γ-hydroxynitriles can be generated from readily available γ-ketonitriles in an efficient and scalable manner, providing a robust and sustainable access to these valuable entities.

item.title: Ring‐Opening Cyclization (ROC) of Aziridines With 2‐(2‐Bromophenyl)‐1H‐Benzimidazoles: Rotamer Analysis and Synthesis of Benzimidazole‐Fused 1,4‐Benzodiazepine
item.description:
A two-step synthetic route to benzimidazole-fused 1,4-benzodiazepines in good to excellent yields via base-mediated nucleophilic ring opening of activated aziridines followed by copper-mediated intramolecular C–N cyclization is developed. Unexpected rotamerism in the ring-opening intermediates was supported by VT-NMR and further substantiated by DFT calculations, providing insight into their conformational dynamics.


We report a novel strategy for the synthesis of benzimidazole-fused 1,4-benzodiazepine derivatives in up to excellent yields via base-mediated nucleophilic ring-opening of activated aziridines with 2-(2-bromophenyl)-1H-benzimidazoles, followed by a Cu-powder-mediated intramolecular C–N cyclization reaction. Conformational isomerism in the ring-opening products due to restricted rotation around the N─C bond was observed. These rotameric compounds were characterized through variable-temperature NMR (VT-NMR) and further supported by DFT calculations.

item.title: Strategic Formation of Indoles Using Phenyl Hydrazine as a Key Reagent
item.description:
Indole formation from phenylhydrazine bridges classical Fischer indolisation with transition-metal-catalyzed and tandem methodologies. This review covers Rh(III), Ru(II), and Co(III)-catalyzed C─H activation, oxidative annulation, and redox-neutral coupling, along with alkyne, alcohol, ester, ketone, carboxamide acid, alkene, cyclic ether, and aldehyde routes to diversely substituted indoles.


Indole formation from phenylhydrazine represents one of the most versatile and mechanistically rich domains in heterocyclic synthesis, bridging classical Fischer indolisation with emerging transition-metal-catalyzed and tandem methodologies. Transition-metal catalysis, such as Rh(III), Ru(II), and Co(III) complexes, has been used for C─H activation, oxidative annulation, and redox-neutral coupling that yield high selectivity and diverse functional group-containing indoles. Moreover, hydroformylation-assisted Fischer reactions, ligand-controlled rearrangements, and acid-promoted condensations have demonstrated controllable C2/C3-substitution and regioselectivity across alkenes, aldehydes, and cyclic precursors. Collectively, these advancements establish phenyl hydrazine as a robust scaffold for the synthesis of multifaceted indoles. This review encompasses alkyne, alcohol, ester, ketone, carboxamide acid, alkene, cyclic ether, and aldehyde routes to diversely substituted indoles.

item.title: [Metal–(Nitrogen and/or OxygenPhosphorus‐Based Ligand)]‐Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydrogenation of β‐Amido β‐Substituted Acrylic Esters and Phosphoro Analogs: A Practical Literature Overview
item.description:
 and/or OxygenPhosphorus-Based Ligand)]-Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydrogenation of β-Amido β-Substituted Acrylic Esters and Phosphoro Analogs: A Practical Literature Overview"/>

Transition-metal-complex-catalyzed asymmetric CC hydrogenation of β-amido β-substituted acrylic esters, phosphonates, and phosphine oxide analogs has been reviewed featuring the application therein of enantiopure (N and/or O)P-monodentate, bis(N and/or O)P-, and (N and/or O)P,P-bidentate ligands.


The advent in catalysis of enantiopure (N and/or O)P-monodentate, bis(N and/or O)P-, and (N and/or O)P,P-bidentate ligands is recounted. In particular, their transition-metal-complex-enabled enantioselective CC hydrogenation of archetypal β-amido β-(alkyl or aryl)-vinylcarboxylic esters, phosphonates, and phosphine oxide analogs is reviewed. The efficient P-ligands are juxtaposed with their reported attained enantioselectivity per substrate alongside the screening conditions. Additional literature pertaining to the asymmetric hydrogenation of the said phosphonates, employing enantiopure diphosphine ligands, is included.

item.title: Photochemical Synthesis of Dihydropyrido[1,2‐a:3,4‐b′]diindole Derivatives
item.description:
A visible-light-induced cyclization of N-(substituted benzoyl)-tetrahydro-β-carbolines was developed to construct dihydropyrido[1,2-a:3,4-b’]diindole scaffolds. This metal-free, p-toluenesulfonic acid (PTSA)-assisted reaction proceeds under 425 nm LED light in N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) in up to 84% yield, tolerating F, Cl, CF3, and OCH3 substituents and fused rings. Mechanistic studies support a photoexcited H-shift/radical coupling/dehydration pathway.


Herein, we report a photochemical method for the intramolecular cyclization of N-(substituted benzoyl)-1-substituted-1,2,3,4-tetrahydro-β-carbolines. This transformation relies on photoexcitation of the substrate itself in the absence of external photocatalysts, with catalytic p-toluenesulfonic acid (PTSA) facilitating the cyclization process. This reaction provides a straightforward and practical approach for the synthesis of dihydro-pyrido[1,2-a:3,4-b′]diindoles. We investigate the substrate scope by varying substituents at the R 2 and R 9 positions of the starting materials. A variety of dihydro-pyrido[1,2-a:3,4-b′]diindoles were successfully synthesized in moderate to excellent yields (up to 84%). Substrates bearing alkyl, aryl, polysubstituted, and fused-ring moieties are well tolerated. Furthermore, the synthetic practicability of this protocol is validated by a gram-scale reaction.

item.title: Modifying Catalytic Sustainability in Renaud Catalysts: Hints From Aromaticity, Conceptual DFT, and Steric Mapping
item.description:
Replacing precious-metal hydrogenation catalysts with sustainable iron systems is becoming a central challenge in catalysis. This predictive computational study reveals how rational redesign of Knölker-type iron complexes dramatically enhances catalytic performance. By tuning cyclopentadienone substituents and annulated rings, activation barriers are significantly reduced, toward highly efficient, greener hydrogenation catalysis.


Catalytic hydrogenation is a key transformation in the chemical and pharmaceutical industries, traditionally relying on noble-metal catalysts such as palladium, ruthenium, and iridium. However, the scarcity, high cost, and environmental concerns associated with these metals have motivated the search for sustainable alternatives based on abundant first-row transition metals. Among them, Knölker-type iron complexes have emerged as promising candidates for efficient hydrogenation catalysis. This predictive study investigates how structural modifications of the cyclopentadienone ligand of the Renaud ligand and annulated-ring framework affect the catalytic activity of iron-based hydrogenation catalysts. Particular attention is devoted to the catalyst activation process and the rate-determining hydrogenation step. Catalyst activation occurs through CO ligand dissociation promoted by trimethylamine-N-oxide, generating the active iron species. The hydrogenation step, involving molecular hydrogen transfer, represents the highest energetic barrier in the catalytic cycle, although protic solvents such as ethanol or water can facilitate this process. The computational results demonstrate that appropriate substituent and ring modifications substantially lower the activation barriers, leading to improved catalytic efficiency. Parameterization by different techniques was performed to understand reactivity trends and interaction patterns.

item.title: Efficient Synthesis of Cannabinoid Acids
item.description:
In this study, an alternative synthesis of cannabinoid acids was developed based on an O→C acyl rearrangement. Specifically, this strategy involved regioselective bromination followed by halogen–lithium exchange and intramolecular nucleophilic addition, which led to successful carboxylation.


Cannabinoid acids are the carboxylic acid precursors of cannabinoids, which are present in high abundance in fresh cannabis plants. During heating and storage, cannabinoid acids undergo decarboxylation to produce the corresponding cannabinoids. Cannabinoid acids have been prepared through the reaction of cannabinoids with methyl magnesium carbonate (MMC); however, this method has a limited substrate scope, and Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinolic acid cannot be produced using this approach. In this study, an alternative synthesis of cannabinoid acids was developed based on an O→C acyl rearrangement. Specifically, this strategy involved regioselective bromination followed by halogen–lithium exchange and intramolecular nucleophilic addition, which led to successful carboxylation. The key reaction was identified as a regioselective bromination using cyclopentyl methyl ether as the optimal solvent, affording the 2-brominated product in high yield. This rearrangement strategy enabled the efficient synthesis of cannabinoid acids from cannabinoids.

item.title: Advances in NN Bond Formation: Mechanistic Diversity and Emerging Catalytic Strategies
item.description:
N Bond Formation: Mechanistic Diversity and Emerging Catalytic Strategies"/>

This review provides an overview of recent advances in NN bond formation through thermal, photochemical, and electrochemical strategies. Key approaches, including oxidative dehydrogenative coupling, reductive coupling, enzymatic catalysis, and metal-catalyzed nitrene transfer, are discussed with emphasis on reaction design, mechanistic insights, and synthetic applications.


The nitrogen–nitrogen (NN) bond is ubiquitous in organic compounds, yet efficient synthetic strategies for the direct construction of NN bonds remain challenging. Well-known approaches, such as oxidative dehydrogenative coupling (ODC) and reductive coupling (RC), have provided valuable routes for forming NN linkages. Nitrene transfer strategies emerged as a complementary and increasingly versatile platform. The distinct electronic structures of classical closed-shell nitrenoids (Fischer- and Schrock-type), open-shell nitrene radical intermediates, and photochemically generated nitrene species primarily govern NN bond-forming selectivity. The use of electrochemical, photochemical, and biocatalytic approaches continues to expand the scope of sustainable synthetic chemistry. This review summarizes recent advances in ODC, RC, nitrene transfer chemistry, photochemical, electrochemical, and enzymatic approaches for NN bond formation, with particular emphasis on reaction design, mechanistic insights, and synthetic applications.

item.title: Synthesis of Symmetrical Secondary Amines From Aqueous Ammonia and Primary Alcohols Catalyzed by an Iridium Complex
item.description:
